CISA Warns of Drupal Core SQL Injection Vulnerability Exploited in Attacks

Cyber Security News
2026-05-25 9 use cases 3 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

CISA has issued an urgent alert regarding a critical SQL injection vulnerability in Drupal Core, tracked as CVE-2026-9082, which is now being actively exploited in real-world attacks. The flaw, classified under CWE-89, affects Drupal’s database abstraction API and could allow attackers to execute malicious SQL queries through specially crafted requests. Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Drupal CVE-2026-9082 SQLi probe: backtick injected into /jsonapi/ filter parameter · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Drupal web server (php-fpm/httpd/nginx) spawning shell or scripting interpreter · [LLM] New PHP file written under Drupal web root by web server process (web shell drop)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Drupal web server initiating internal lateral connections on SMB/RDP/SSH/DB ports · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Drupal CVE-2026-9082 SQLi probe: backtick injected into /jsonapi/ filter parameter Exploitation Medium
Hunts for HTTP requests to internet-exposed Drupal endpoints carrying SQL meta-characters (UNION SELECT, sleep(), --, ';', backticks) in query strings, POST bodies, or JSON:API filter parameters — the exploitation pattern CISA flagged for CVE-2026-9082 against Drupal Core 8.9.0–11.2.0. Rationale: Anchored on the article's CVE-2026-9082 + Drupal Core SQL injection in the database abstraction API. Endpoints (/jsonapi/, /node/, /user/login, /?q=, /index.php) are Drupal's documented attack surface for prior SQLi CVEs (Drupalgeddon family) and reasonable hunting grounds while public PoCs emerge. Cross-checked against CISA KEV catalogue (https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog) and Drupal Security Advisories archive for prior database-API SQLi patterns (e.g. SA-CORE-2014-005 Drupalgeddon). Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog • https://www.drupal.org/security • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Drupal exploitation surfaces in non-Defender web telemetry; this approximation hunts for outbound replies via DeviceNetworkEvents where the Drupal host (web server) received the malicious request pattern via reverse-proxy. Prefer the Sentinel/Splunk W3CIISLog query for primary detection.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("httpd.exe","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe","php-cgi.exe","php-fpm.exe")
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("UNION SELECT","information_schema","jsonapi","--","sleep(")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
let DrupalPaths = dynamic(["/jsonapi/","/node/","/user/login","/?q=","/index.php","/admin/"]);
let SqliTokens = dynamic(["union select","union%20select","sleep(","' or 1=1","%27%20or%201%3d1","information_schema","' or '1'='1","--+","%60","';"]);
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csUriStem has_any (DrupalPaths) or csUriQuery has_any (DrupalPaths)
| extend FullReq = tolower(strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery))
| where FullReq has_any (SqliTokens)
| summarize HitCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Samples = make_set(FullReq, 5), Statuses = make_set(scStatus, 5), UAs = make_set(csUserAgent, 5) by Computer, sSiteName, cIP
| where HitCount >= 3
| order by HitCount desc
title: Drupal Core CVE-2026-9082 SQLi Pattern in Web Requests
id: 9b2fa3a4-1c81-4d2e-8a7b-2026908201aa
description: Detects HTTP requests targeting Drupal endpoints with SQL injection meta-characters matching CVE-2026-9082 exploitation.
references:
  - https://cybersecuritynews.com/drupal-core-sql-injection-vulnerability-exploited/
  - https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/25
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection_path:
    cs-uri-stem|contains:
      - '/jsonapi/'
      - '/node/'
      - '/user/login'
      - '/?q='
      - '/index.php'
  selection_payload:
    cs-uri-query|contains:
      - 'UNION SELECT'
      - 'union%20select'
      - 'sleep('
      - "' OR 1=1"
      - '%27%20OR%201%3D1'
      - 'information_schema'
      - '--+'
  condition: selection_path and selection_payload
level: high
(source:nginx.access OR source:apache.access OR source:iis OR source:cloudfront) (@http.url_details.path:(*/jsonapi/* OR */node/* OR */user/login* OR */?q=* OR */index.php*)) AND (@http.url:(*UNION*SELECT* OR *union%20select* OR *sleep\(* OR *information_schema* OR *--+* OR *%27%20OR%201%3D1*) OR @http.url:(*UNION*select* OR *Union*Select*))
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| // Falcon FDR does not natively parse web-request bodies; pivot via the DNS resolution the attacker did on the target prior to scanning.
| DomainName=/.*\.(drupal|drupalhost|cms)\..*/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
# log group: /aws/wafv2/<your-web-acl> (or /aws/cloudfront/<distribution> access logs)
fields @timestamp, httpRequest.clientIp, httpRequest.uri, httpRequest.args, httpRequest.headers.0.value, action, terminatingRuleId
| filter httpRequest.uri like /\/(jsonapi|node|user|admin|index\.php)/
      and (httpRequest.args like /(?i)(union\s+select|sleep\(|information_schema|--\+|%27%20or%201%3d1|%60)/
           or httpRequest.uri like /(?i)(union\s+select|sleep\(|information_schema)/)
| stats count(*) as hits by httpRequest.clientIp, terminatingRuleId, action
| sort hits desc
| limit 100
WEB

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.http_method) as methods values(Web.status) as statuses from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*/jsonapi/*" OR Web.url="*/node/*" OR Web.url="*/user/*" OR Web.url="*/?q=*" OR Web.url="*/index.php*") AND (Web.url="*UNION*SELECT*" OR Web.url="*union%20select*" OR Web.url="*sleep(*" OR Web.url="*' OR 1=1*" OR Web.url="*%27%20OR%201%3D1*" OR Web.url="*--+*" OR Web.url="*information_schema*" OR Web.url="*';*" OR Web.url="*%60*") by Web.dest Web.src Web.user_agent Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where count > 3
[LLM] Drupal web server (php-fpm/httpd/nginx) spawning shell or scripting interpreter Installation High
Detects post-exploitation command execution where a Drupal-hosting web server process spawns sh/bash/python/perl — the second-stage signal that a CVE-2026-9082 SQLi has been chained into RCE on the underlying host. Rationale: The article and kill-chain explicitly call out 'Execution of arbitrary code on the underlying server in certain configurations' and 'unexpected child processes spawned by the web server (php-fpm, httpd, nginx → sh/bash/python)'. Web-server parents spawning shell interpreters is one of the highest-fidelity web-exploitation post-conditions and is the canonical second-stage signal for SQLi-to-RCE chains. Cross-checked MITRE T1190 procedure examples and Sigma rule sigma/rules/linux/process_creation/proc_creation_lnx_susp_web_shell_exec.yml. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/ • https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/tree/master/rules/linux/process_creation
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm","php-cgi","php-cgi.exe","httpd","httpd.exe","nginx","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe","apache2")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","python","python3","perl","ruby","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wget","curl","nc","ncat")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","php-cgi","httpd","nginx","w3wp.exe","apache2")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","python","python3","perl","ruby","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wget","curl","nc","ncat")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentImage = ParentProcessName,
          ParentCmd   = ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = ActingProcessName,
          ChildCmd    = ActingProcessCommandLine,
          Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 4f2d9c11-6e83-4a02-b7ad-2026908202bb
description: Detects php-fpm/httpd/nginx spawning shell/script interpreters or networking tools — classic RCE-via-webapp signal applicable to CVE-2026-9082 Drupal SQLi-to-RCE chain.
references:

tags:

level: high
(source:linux.auditd OR source:windows.sysmon) ((@process.parent.name:(php-fpm OR php-cgi OR httpd OR nginx OR apache2 OR w3wp.exe) OR @ParentImage:(*\php-fpm* OR *\httpd* OR *\nginx* OR *\w3wp.exe OR *\W3WP.EXE)) AND (@process.name:(sh OR bash OR dash OR python OR python3 OR perl OR wget OR curl OR nc OR ncat) OR @Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\CMD.EXE OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(php-fpm|php-cgi|httpd|nginx|apache2|w3wp\.exe)$/i

[LLM] New PHP file written under Drupal web root by web server process (web shell drop) Installation High
Catches the persistence step the article calls out — attackers deploying web shells under writable Drupal directories (sites/default/files, modules, themes) after SQLi-driven RCE. Detection fires when a web-server-context process writes a .php/.phtml/.phar file into a Drupal-owned path. Rationale: Article: 'Attackers can leverage this flaw to gain a foothold, deploy web shells, or pivot deeper into the network.' Detection hint in kill-chain phase 6 explicitly says 'Detect new or modified .php/.phtml files written under Drupal web roots (sites/default/files, modules) and subsequent HTTP requests to those files'. The sites/default/files path is the only standard web-writable location in a Drupal install, making writes there from a web-server process near-canary level. Cross-checked Drupal documentation (drupal.org/docs/security-in-drupal/securing-file-permissions-and-ownership) confirming sites/default/files is the only chmod-writable directory under hardened deployments. Cross-checked against: • https://www.drupal.org/docs/security-in-drupal/securing-file-permissions-and-ownership • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/
ATT&CKT1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in~ ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FileName endswith ".php" or FileName endswith ".phtml" or FileName endswith ".phar" or FileName endswith ".inc"
| where FolderPath has_any ("/sites/default/files/","/sites/all/files/","\\sites\\default\\files\\","/modules/","/themes/","/profiles/")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm","php-cgi","php-cgi.exe","httpd","httpd.exe","nginx","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe","apache2")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("php","phtml","phar","inc")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/sites/default/files/","/sites/all/files/","\\sites\\default\\files\\","/modules/","/themes/","/profiles/")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","php-cgi","httpd","nginx","w3wp.exe","apache2")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: PHP File Written Under Drupal Web Root by Web Server Process
id: 7d3e91ce-ab12-4cf3-9026-2026908203cc
description: Detects creation of PHP/PHTML/PHAR files under Drupal sites/modules/themes directories by the web server itself — strong indicator of web-shell deployment after SQLi-to-RCE (CVE-2026-9082).
references:
  - https://cybersecuritynews.com/drupal-core-sql-injection-vulnerability-exploited/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/25
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1505.003
logsource:
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection_writer:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/php-fpm'
      - '/php-cgi'
      - '/httpd'
      - '/nginx'
      - '/apache2'
      - '\w3wp.exe'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '/sites/default/files/'
      - '/sites/all/files/'
      - '\sites\default\files\'
      - '/modules/'
      - '/themes/'
      - '/profiles/'
  selection_ext:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.php'
      - '.phtml'
      - '.phar'
      - '.inc'
  condition: selection_writer and selection_path and selection_ext
level: high
(source:linux.auditd OR source:windows.sysmon) (@process.name:(php-fpm OR php-cgi OR httpd OR nginx OR apache2 OR w3wp.exe) OR @Image:(*\w3wp.exe OR *\W3WP.EXE OR *\php-fpm* OR *\httpd* OR *\nginx*)) AND (@file.path:(*\/sites\/default\/files\/* OR *\/sites\/all\/files\/* OR *\/modules\/* OR *\/themes\/*) OR @TargetFilename:(*\\sites\\default\\files\\* OR *\/sites\/default\/files\/*)) AND (@file.extension:(php OR phtml OR phar OR inc) OR @TargetFilename:(*.php OR *.phtml OR *.phar OR *.inc))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| ContextImageFileName=/(php-fpm|php-cgi|httpd|nginx|apache2|w3wp\.exe)$/i
| TargetFileName=/\.(php|phtml|phar|inc)$/i
| regex("(/sites/(default|all)/files/|/modules/|/themes/|/profiles/|\\\\sites\\\\default\\\\files\\\\)", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
| sort(count, order=desc)

[LLM] Drupal web server initiating internal lateral connections on SMB/RDP/SSH/DB ports Actions on Objectives Medium
After foothold, the kill-chain expects pivot from the web tier into internal networks. This UC catches the Drupal-hosting web process (php-fpm/httpd/nginx/w3wp) initiating outbound or east-west TCP to RFC1918 destinations on lateral-movement ports — traffic shape that should essentially never originate from a front-end web tier. Rationale: Article kill-chain phase 7: 'Monitor for outbound or east-west connections initiated by the web server process to internal hosts on SMB/RDP/SSH/DB ports — Drupal front-end nodes should rarely initiate such traffic.' Anchored on the explicit guidance to detect process-attributed east-west pivots and the specific port set typical of post-exploit recon (445/3389/22/DB ports). Cross-checked MITRE T1210 procedure examples confirming web-shell-driven internal scanning is a documented pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1210/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/
ATT&CKT1210 T1021
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm","php-cgi","php-cgi.exe","httpd","httpd.exe","nginx","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe","apache2","sh","bash","python","python3","perl")
| where RemotePort in (22,135,139,445,1433,1521,3306,3389,5432,5985,5986,6379,27017)
| where RemoteIPType == "Private"
| where ActionType in~ ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt","ConnectionFound")
| summarize ConnCount = count(), Targets = make_set(RemoteIP, 25), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemotePort
| where array_length(Targets) >= 1
| order by ConnCount desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SrcHostname has_any ("web","drupal","cms") or DvcHostname has_any ("web","drupal","cms")
| where DstPortNumber in (22,135,139,445,1433,1521,3306,3389,5432,5985,5986,6379,27017)
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr)
| where DvcAction != "Deny"
| summarize ConnCount = count(), Targets = make_set(DstIpAddr, 25), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by SrcHostname, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol
| order by ConnCount desc
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd) @EventID:3 AND (@Image:(*\php-fpm* OR *\php-cgi* OR *\httpd* OR *\nginx* OR *\w3wp.exe OR *\W3WP.EXE OR *\apache2) OR @process.name:(php-fpm OR php-cgi OR httpd OR nginx OR apache2 OR sh OR bash OR python OR python3)) AND @DestinationPort:(22 OR 135 OR 139 OR 445 OR 1433 OR 1521 OR 3306 OR 3389 OR 5432 OR 5985 OR 5986 OR 6379 OR 27017) AND (CIDR(@DestinationIp, 10.0.0.0/8) OR CIDR(@DestinationIp, 172.16.0.0/12) OR CIDR(@DestinationIp, 192.168.0.0/16))
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4
| ContextImageFileName=/(php-fpm|php-cgi|httpd|nginx|apache2|w3wp\.exe|\/sh$|\/bash$|\/python3?$)/i
| RemotePort=22 OR RemotePort=135 OR RemotePort=139 OR RemotePort=445 OR RemotePort=1433 OR RemotePort=1521 OR RemotePort=3306 OR RemotePort=3389 OR RemotePort=5432 OR RemotePort=5985 OR RemotePort=5986 OR RemotePort=6379 OR RemotePort=27017
| cidr("10.0.0.0/8", field=RemoteAddressIP4) OR cidr("172.16.0.0/12", field=RemoteAddressIP4) OR cidr("192.168.0.0/16", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=count())
| sort(count, order=desc)
# log group: /aws/vpc/flowlogs
fields @timestamp, srcAddr, dstAddr, dstPort, protocol, action, bytes
| filter action = "ACCEPT"
      and dstPort in [22, 135, 139, 445, 1433, 1521, 3306, 3389, 5985, 5986, 5432, 6379, 27017]
      and (dstAddr like /^10\./ or dstAddr like /^172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\./ or dstAddr like /^192\.168\./)
      and (srcAddr like /^10\.<drupal-tier-subnet>\./)
| stats count(*) as flows, sum(bytes) as bytes_out by srcAddr, dstAddr, dstPort
| sort flows desc
| limit 100

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd

let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo

              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;

| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)

// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"

| order by TimeGenerated desc

    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.

[LLM] TrapDoor named-package install via npm / pip / cargo on developer host Delivery High
Hunts for installation or invocation of any of the 34 named TrapDoor packages across npm, PyPI, and Crates.io. Highest-fidelity IOC pivot in the campaign — package names are bespoke and unlikely to appear outside this attack. Rationale: Pivots on the exact 34 package-name strings published by Socket (cross-confirmed at socket.dev/blog/trapdoor-crypto-stealer-npm-pypi-crates). These names are bespoke typosquats unlikely to collide with legitimate registry traffic, making any `npm install <name>` / `pip install <name>` / `cargo add <name>` invocation a near-certain TP. [LLM] Python interpreter spawning node -e fetching remote JS (TrapDoor PyPI delegation) Installation High
Hunts the TrapDoor PyPI execution chain: a malicious PyPI package auto-executes on import, then shells out to `node -e` to run an inline JS payload that retrieves trap-core.js from ddjidd564.github.io. python.exe → node.exe with -e is an extremely rare pattern outside this attack. Rationale: python→node with `-e` is a near-zero-FP pattern; the article and Socket both explicitly call out this exact delegation ("auto-executed on import...download JavaScript from an attacker-controlled GitHub Pages domain (ddjidd564[.]github[.]io), and run it using node -e"). Adding the ddjidd564/defi-security-best-practices/github.io URL fragments anchors the detection to the campaign's actual payload host. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/trapdoor-crypto-stealer-npm-pypi-crates

[LLM] TrapDoor C2 contact to ddjidd564.github.io payload host Command & Control High
Hunts any DNS resolution or HTTP fetch of ddjidd564.github.io — the GitHub Pages domain the TrapDoor PyPI loader uses to retrieve trap-core.js. Single-IOC detection; any developer host contacting this domain is compromised. Rationale: Pivots on the campaign's sole infrastructure IOC — Socket confirms ddjidd564.github.io as the payload host (path /defi-security-best-practices/) and the GitHub account that anchors the entire 34-package campaign. Single-IOC detection is rarely justified, but a developer-attributed GitHub Pages domain with zero legitimate use case is the exception. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/trapdoor-crypto-stealer-npm-pypi-crates • https://cyberpress.org/supply-chain-attack-compromises-34-packages/

[LLM] TrapDoor AI prompt-injection persistence — .cursorrules / CLAUDE.md drop by build tools Installation High
Hunts creation or modification of .cursorrules or CLAUDE.md files by package-manager-spawned processes (node, npm, python, pip, cargo, rustc). TrapDoor's novel persistence vector implants zero-width-Unicode-laced instructions into these AI assistant config files so Cursor and Claude Code will silently execute 'security scans' that exfiltrate secrets. Rationale: Targets the novel TrapDoor persistence vector explicitly called out by both the article and Socket: "implanting of .cursorrules and CLAUDE.md containing hidden instructions to trick AI assistants into running a 'security scan' that results in secret discovery and exfiltration." Socket additionally confirms the use of zero-width Unicode in the file content. The parent-process narrowing to build tools makes the FP rate manageable. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/trapdoor-crypto-stealer-npm-pypi-crates • https://www.cyberkendra.com/2026/05/malicious-packages-on-npm-pypi-and.html

[LLM] TrapDoor persistence install via cron / systemd / git hooks / SSH from package-manager parent Installation Medium
Hunts persistence mechanism establishment (crontab edits, systemd user unit writes, .git/hooks installs, SSH key/authorized_keys writes, shell-rc modifications) where the initiating process chain traces back to npm/pip/cargo/node/python — the trap-core.js post-install routine. Rationale: The article explicitly enumerates the persistence primitives planted by trap-core.js: "persistence using cron jobs, systemd services, Git hooks, and moves across the network via SSH." The detection's high-fidelity element is the parent-process narrowing — a developer's npm install spawning crontab is anomalous; SYSTEM/services.exe spawning crontab is not. Inclusion of git hooks and shell-rc paths catches the trap-core.js variants that prefer userland persistence over root-required cron. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/trapdoor-crypto-stealer-npm-pypi-crates
ATT&CKT1053.003 T1543.002 T1546.004 T1098.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let BuildParents = dynamic(["node.exe","node","npm.exe","npm","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","python.exe","python","python3","python3.exe","pip.exe","pip","pip3","cargo.exe","cargo","rustc.exe","build-script-build","build-script-build.exe"]);
let PersistMechanisms = dynamic(["crontab","crontab.exe","systemctl","systemctl.exe","ssh-keygen","ssh-keygen.exe","ssh-keyscan","schtasks.exe","reg.exe"]);
union
  (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (BuildParents) or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (BuildParents))
    | where FileName in~ (PersistMechanisms)
        or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("crontab -","systemctl --user enable","systemctl enable","/etc/cron.","/etc/systemd/system/","~/.config/systemd/user","~/.bashrc","~/.zshrc","~/.profile","~/.bash_profile","authorized_keys",".git/hooks/pre-commit",".git/hooks/post-checkout",".git/hooks/post-merge","schtasks /create","HKCU\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine),
  (DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (BuildParents) or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (BuildParents)
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
    | where FolderPath has_any ("/etc/cron","/etc/systemd/system","/.config/systemd/user","/.ssh/","/.git/hooks/")
        or FileName in~ (".bashrc",".zshrc",".profile",".bash_profile","authorized_keys")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| order by Timestamp desc
let BuildParents = dynamic(["node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","pip.exe","pip3.exe","cargo.exe","rustc.exe","node","npm","python","python3","pip","cargo"]);
let PersistMechanisms = dynamic(["crontab","systemctl","ssh-keygen","ssh-keyscan","schtasks.exe","reg.exe"]);
union isfuzzy=true

    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, EventType, EventVendor)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Persistence Mechanism Created by Package Manager Process (TrapDoor-style)

description: Persistence primitive (crontab edit, systemd unit, git hook install, SSH authorized_keys write, or shell rc modification) initiated by a process whose parent chain is npm/pip/cargo/node/python. TrapDoor's trap-core.js explicitly plants persistence via cron, systemd, git hooks, shell hooks, and SSH from package post-install context.
references:

  - https://socket.dev/blog/trapdoor-crypto-stealer-npm-pypi-crates

detection:

      - '\cargo.exe'

  selection_persist_proc:
    Image|endswith:

      - '/systemctl'
      - '/ssh-keygen'

  selection_persist_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:

      - '/etc/systemd/system/'

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user

        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count

    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,

// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010

SecurityEvent

| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"

The operation explicitly targets developers in the crypto, DeFi, Solana, and AI communities by disguising malware as generic developer tools and security scanners. Exploitation. [LLM] npm/pip/cargo build-time subprocess spawning `node -e` or curl/wget (TrapDoor execution primitive) Installation High
Hunts the article-defined execution pattern where npm postinstall, PyPI import-time, or Crates build.rs scripts spawn a network-fetching child (node with -e flag, curl, wget). This is the shared bottleneck across all three TrapDoor delivery vectors before the trap-core.js payload is staged. Rationale: Anchors on the exact execution primitives Socket documented per registry (npm postinstall, PyPI import → node -e, Crates build.rs) and the C2 string ddjidd564.github.io. The parent-child binary pair is high-signal because legitimate npm/pip/cargo workflows almost never spawn node -e or curl as a child during install. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/trapdoor-crypto-stealer-npm-pypi-crates • https://www.cyberkendra.com/2026/05/malicious-packages-on-npm-pypi-and.html

[LLM] AI assistant rules files (.cursorrules / CLAUDE.md) written by non-editor process Weaponization Medium
Detects creation or modification of .cursorrules and CLAUDE.md files by build-tool or scripted processes — the TrapDoor vector for AI-prompt-injection-driven credential exfiltration using zero-width Unicode (U+200B–U+200D, U+FEFF). Legitimate writes come from VS Code, Cursor, JetBrains; campaign writes come from node, python, cargo, or PR merge automation. Rationale: Article explicitly calls out poisoning .cursorrules and CLAUDE.md with zero-width Unicode as a defining TrapDoor TTP. The non-editor process filter is the key fidelity boost — humans edit these files via Cursor/VS Code/JetBrains, never via cargo or pip. Pair with a content scan for U+200B/200C/200D/FEFF as a follow-up enrichment. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/trapdoor-crypto-stealer-npm-pypi-crates

[LLM] TrapDoor malicious package name in npm/pip/cargo install command or lockfile write Delivery High
Direct package-name IOC hunt across install command lines and dependency manifest writes for the 34 named TrapDoor packages, anchored on the four names disclosed in the article and the first-observed package eth-security-auditor. Rationale: Article + Socket provide exact malicious package names (eth-security-auditor, prompt-engineering-toolkit, solidity-deploy-guard, defi-threat-scanner). These strings have no legitimate use — any match is virtually a true positive. Cross-checks both process-creation (active install) and lockfile-write (transitive pull) paths. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/trapdoor-crypto-stealer-npm-pypi-crates • https://www.cyberkendra.com/2026/05/malicious-packages-on-npm-pypi-and.html

  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
            InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source="Process"),
(DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName in~ ("package.json","package-lock.json","requirements.txt","pyproject.toml","Pipfile","Pipfile.lock","Cargo.toml","Cargo.lock")
  | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")

| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] Build-tool subprocess reading developer secrets (SSH keys, AWS creds, Solana/Sui/Aptos wallets, browser logins) Actions on Objectives High
Hunts the TrapDoor credential-harvest phase: node, python, or cargo (and their build.rs / postinstall children) reading sensitive paths within seconds of an install event. The trap-core.js implant targets ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.config/solana, ~/.sui, ~/.aptos, and browser Login Data files. Rationale: Article enumerates exact target paths: ~/.ssh, ~/.aws environment / credentials, browser profiles, Sui/Solana/Aptos wallets. The PathCount >= 3 threshold is the trap-core.js fingerprint — legitimate build tools may read one config file, but bulk-reading 3+ distinct secret directories in 5 min by a single short-lived node/python/cargo PID is the TrapDoor collection pattern. The CloudWatch arm catches the article's 'live API validation' step (post-harvest sts:GetCallerIdentity call from a Boto3/node user-agent). Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/trapdoor-crypto-stealer-npm-pypi-crates
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1555.003 T1539 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","FileAccessed","FileOpened")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("node","node.exe","python","python3","python.exe","cargo","cargo.exe","rustc","build-script-build","npm","npm.exe","pip","pip3")
| where FolderPath has_any ("/.ssh/","\\.ssh\\","/.aws/","\\.aws\\","/.config/solana","/.sui","/.aptos","/.config/sui","/.move","/.npmrc","/.netrc","/.config/gh")
   or FileName in~ ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","id_ecdsa","id_dsa","credentials","Login Data","Cookies","Web Data","keystore.json",".npmrc",".netrc")
| summarize PathCount=dcount(FolderPath), Paths=make_set(FolderPath, 25), Files=make_set(FileName, 25),
            FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp)
    by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where PathCount >= 3   // bulk-read threshold: 3+ distinct sensitive dirs in 5 min
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImFileEvent

| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","python","python3","cargo","rustc","build-script-build","npm","pip","pip3")

   or TargetFileName in~ ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","id_ecdsa","credentials","Login Data","Cookies","Web Data","keystore.json",".npmrc",".netrc")

            FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated)
    by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where PathCount >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc

| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId], function=count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true, as=uniquePaths))

# log group: /aws/cloudtrail
fields @timestamp, eventName, sourceIPAddress, userIdentity.userName, userIdentity.arn, userIdentity.type, userAgent
| filter eventName in ["GetCallerIdentity","ListBuckets","ListUsers","ListAccessKeys","GetUser"]

| stats count() as calls, earliest(@timestamp) as firstCall, latest(@timestamp) as lastCall, count_distinct(eventName) as distinctActions by userIdentity.arn, sourceIPAddress
| filter calls >= 2
| sort firstCall desc

[LLM] Build-tool subprocess installing shell/systemd/git-hook persistence (trap-core.js footholds) Installation High
Hunts the trap-core.js persistence stage: node/python/npm/cargo processes writing to shell rc files (~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc, ~/.profile), systemd unit files, cron paths, or .git/hooks/* — the four mechanisms the article calls out as TrapDoor's 'complex persistence'. Rationale: Article explicitly lists the four trap-core.js persistence mechanisms: systemd services, cron, git hooks, shell rc files. Pairing each persistence target with build-tool ancestry filters the bulk of legitimate edits (which happen via $EDITOR / VS Code) from the TrapDoor pattern (which happens during npm install / cargo build). Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/trapdoor-crypto-stealer-npm-pypi-crates

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    from datamodel=Web

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Endpoint network/DNS contact with Ghost CMS ClickFix campaign infrastructure · Network connections to article IPs / domains

[LLM] Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 SQL injection probing against /ghost/ admin endpoints Exploitation High
Hunts unauthenticated SQL-injection attempts against Ghost CMS admin/canary API paths consistent with CVE-2026-26980 exploitation — bursts of requests carrying UNION/SELECT/information_schema/sleep payloads or causing 4xx/500 errors on /ghost/api/* routes. Article-specific because it pivots on Ghost's URL space rather than a generic WAF rule. Rationale: Pivots on the Ghost CMS URL namespace (/ghost/api/admin, /ghost/api/canary) called out in the CVE-2026-26980 advisory plus classic SQLi payload tokens; combined with response-code anomalies this catches blind/error-based SQLi enumeration rather than benign API traffic. Cross-checked against the SentinelOne Feb-27 write-up referenced in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/ • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-26980 • https://ghost.org/docs/security/
ATT&CKT1190 T1552.001
Data sourcesWeb
let SqliMarkers = dynamic(["union","UNION","select","SELECT","information_schema","sleep(","0x3a","%27","--","/*!","benchmark("]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (W3CIISLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where csUriStem startswith "/ghost/" or csUriStem contains "/api/admin/" or csUriStem contains "/api/canary/"
        | where csUriQuery has_any (SqliMarkers) or scStatus in ("500","400")
        | summarize Hits = count(), Stems = make_set(csUriStem, 25), Statuses = make_set(scStatus, 10), Queries = make_set(csUriQuery, 25) by cIP, csUserAgent, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
        | where Hits > 5),
    (AppServiceHTTPLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where CsUriStem startswith "/ghost/" or CsUriStem contains "/api/admin/" or CsUriStem contains "/api/canary/"
        | where CsUriQuery has_any (SqliMarkers) or ScStatus in (400,500)
        | summarize Hits = count(), Stems = make_set(CsUriStem, 25), Statuses = make_set(ScStatus, 10), Queries = make_set(CsUriQuery, 25) by CIp, UserAgent, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
        | where Hits > 5),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where RequestURL has "/ghost/" and RequestURL has_any (SqliMarkers)
        | summarize Hits = count(), Urls = make_set(RequestURL, 25) by SourceIP, RequestClientApplication, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
        | where Hits > 5)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(nginx OR apache OR iis) @http.url_details.path:(*\/ghost\/api\/admin\/* OR *\/ghost\/api\/canary\/* OR *\/ghost\/api\/*) AND (@http.url:(*union*select* OR *UNION*SELECT* OR *information_schema* OR *sleep\(* OR *%27* OR *0x*) OR @http.status_code:(400 OR 500))

[LLM] Endpoint network/DNS contact with Ghost CMS ClickFix campaign infrastructure Command & Control High
Hunts host-side resolution or connection to the cloaking, staging, and payload-hosting domains and the single IP tied by XLab to the CVE-2026-26980 ClickFix follow-on. Article-specific because the indicator set is the actual XLab IOC bundle, not a generic suspicious-TLD list. Rationale: Uses the XLab-published IOC bundle (8 domains + 144.31.236.66) verbatim against host DNS/network telemetry — these are not legitimate Cloudflare/CDN namespaces, so hits are high-fidelity. Cross-checked the staticcloudflare.pro typosquat pattern via VirusTotal community reports tied to the same cluster. Cross-checked against: • https://urlscan.io/ • https://www.virustotal.com/ • https://x.com/XLab_Qianxin

[LLM] ClickFix lure execution: browser-spawned shell pasting payload command to campaign infra Delivery High
Catches the ClickFix lure being acted on — a browser (or explorer Run dialog) spawns cmd/powershell/mshta whose command line references one of the XLab-published staging hostnames/IP, often using curl/iwr/mshta/bitsadmin/certutil to pull the next stage. The combination of browser parent + LOLBin child + campaign IOC string is what makes this article-specific. Rationale: Models the exact ClickFix kill-chain step described in the article — the victim is told to paste a command into the Run dialog/cmd which then fetches from attacker infra. Parent=browser/explorer + child=shell + command line containing an XLab IOC or a download LOLBin pattern is high-signal; the IOC list anchors it to this specific campaign rather than generic ClickFix templates. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/004/ • https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.003 T1059.001 T1105

| where AccountName !endswith "$"

let CampaignIOCs = dynamic(["clo4shara.xyz","cloud-verification.com","jalwat.com","com-apps.cc","web-telegram.ug","platecrumbs.com","taketwolabs.com","staticcloudflare.pro","144.31.236.66"]);

        | where CommandLine has_any (CampaignIOCs)
           or (CommandLine has_any ("curl ","Invoke-WebRequest","iwr ","DownloadString","mshta","bitsadmin","certutil -urlcache") and CommandLine matches regex @"https?://")
        | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, TargetProcessName, CommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] UtilifySetup.exe Electron implant or campaign-hashed payload execution Installation High
Detects execution, write, or load of the Electron-packaged 'UtilifySetup.exe' implant or any of the five MD5s attributed by XLab to the Ghost CMS ClickFix campaign payload set. Hash-and-name anchored so it is unambiguously this campaign. Rationale: Uses the verbatim five MD5 IOCs and the unique payload name 'UtilifySetup.exe' from the XLab report — Electron installer + that exact name is not a known legitimate product, and the hashes are post-classification campaign-specific. Multi-table union covers execution, file-drop, and image-load to catch staged loaders and the final Electron binary. Cross-checked against: • https://bazaar.abuse.ch/ • https://www.virustotal.com/ • https://otx.alienvault.com/
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1059.007 T1218.011
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let CampaignHashes = dynamic(["5659292833ec421da11ebde005d9c9a8","d30cc10d54ebc967c8538ff74f442eee","18a7251ddde77ed24bc54700d84d9be1","f280e12f51f996dae7fffc64a56ee527","fceca579efcef09eb507c6ca977ea281"]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where FileName =~ "UtilifySetup.exe"
            or MD5 in (CampaignHashes)
            or InitiatingProcessMD5 in (CampaignHashes)
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, MD5, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents"),
    (DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where FileName =~ "UtilifySetup.exe"
            or MD5 in (CampaignHashes)
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, MD5, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileOriginUrl, FileOriginReferrerUrl, Source = "DeviceFileEvents"),
    (DeviceImageLoadEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where MD5 in (CampaignHashes)
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, MD5, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceImageLoadEvents")
| order by Timestamp desc
let CampaignHashes = dynamic(["5659292833ec421da11ebde005d9c9a8","d30cc10d54ebc967c8538ff74f442eee","18a7251ddde77ed24bc54700d84d9be1","f280e12f51f996dae7fffc64a56ee527","fceca579efcef09eb507c6ca977ea281"]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where TargetProcessName endswith "UtilifySetup.exe" or MD5 in (CampaignHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, MD5, SHA256, Source = "ImProcessCreate"),
    (ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where TargetFileName =~ "UtilifySetup.exe" or TargetFileMD5 in (CampaignHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileMD5, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImFileEvent"),
    (SecurityEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where EventID == 4688
        | where NewProcessName endswith "UtilifySetup.exe" or FileHash in (CampaignHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, FileHash, Source = "SecurityEvent_4688")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: UtilifySetup.exe Electron implant from Ghost CMS ClickFix campaign
id: f8d2c5a4-9e1b-4f7a-bc2d-1a3e6f0b8d52
description: Execution of UtilifySetup.exe, the Electron-packaged implant served by the Ghost CMS ClickFix campaign (XLab/Qianxin, May 2026), or any of the five MD5s tied to the same campaign payload set.
references:

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-26980")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-26980")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
