Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("5659292833ec421da11ebde005d9c9a8", "d30cc10d54ebc967c8538ff74f442eee", "18a7251ddde77ed24bc54700d84d9be1", "f280e12f51f996dae7fffc64a56ee527", "fceca579efcef09eb507c6ca977ea281") or SHA1 in~ ("5659292833ec421da11ebde005d9c9a8", "d30cc10d54ebc967c8538ff74f442eee", "18a7251ddde77ed24bc54700d84d9be1", "f280e12f51f996dae7fffc64a56ee527", "fceca579efcef09eb507c6ca977ea281") or MD5 in~ ("5659292833ec421da11ebde005d9c9a8", "d30cc10d54ebc967c8538ff74f442eee", "18a7251ddde77ed24bc54700d84d9be1", "f280e12f51f996dae7fffc64a56ee527", "fceca579efcef09eb507c6ca977ea281")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("5659292833ec421da11ebde005d9c9a8", "d30cc10d54ebc967c8538ff74f442eee", "18a7251ddde77ed24bc54700d84d9be1", "f280e12f51f996dae7fffc64a56ee527", "fceca579efcef09eb507c6ca977ea281") or SHA1 in~ ("5659292833ec421da11ebde005d9c9a8", "d30cc10d54ebc967c8538ff74f442eee", "18a7251ddde77ed24bc54700d84d9be1", "f280e12f51f996dae7fffc64a56ee527", "fceca579efcef09eb507c6ca977ea281") or MD5 in~ ("5659292833ec421da11ebde005d9c9a8", "d30cc10d54ebc967c8538ff74f442eee", "18a7251ddde77ed24bc54700d84d9be1", "f280e12f51f996dae7fffc64a56ee527", "fceca579efcef09eb507c6ca977ea281")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["5659292833ec421da11ebde005d9c9a8", "d30cc10d54ebc967c8538ff74f442eee", "18a7251ddde77ed24bc54700d84d9be1", "f280e12f51f996dae7fffc64a56ee527", "fceca579efcef09eb507c6ca977ea281"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Malicious helpers.php dropped under vendor/laravel-lang/ during Composer install · [LLM] Composer command line installing or updating laravel-lang/* packages (scope hunt)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] PHP / Composer spawns executable from %TEMP% (DebugElevator dropper) · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Laravel Lang packages hijacked to deploy credential-stealing malware
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] C2 callback to Laravel Lang stealer infrastructure (flipboxstudio.info) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Chromium Local State / Login Data accessed by non-browser binary from %TEMP% (App-Bound Encryption theft) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
[LLM] C2 callback to Laravel Lang stealer infrastructure (flipboxstudio.info) Command & Control High
Detects any DNS resolution or outbound HTTP(S) connection to flipboxstudio.info, the attacker-controlled C2 used by the hijacked Laravel Lang Composer packages to pull the second-stage PHP credential stealer and exfiltrate harvested secrets. Any hit on a developer workstation or CI runner is high-fidelity confirmed compromise. Rationale: flipboxstudio.info is the only network IOC in the article and is named both as the dropper-pull host and the encrypted-exfil sink. A single hit equals confirmed install of the trojanised laravel-lang package on that host — the only reason a corporate endpoint resolves this domain.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105 T1041

[LLM] PHP / Composer spawns executable from %TEMP% (DebugElevator dropper) Installation High
Detects php.exe or php-cgi.exe spawning a *.exe child located under %TEMP% — the exact behaviour of the Laravel Lang stealer's PHP stage, which base64-decodes the embedded DebugElevator Windows binary, writes it to %TEMP% under a random filename, and launches it to crack Chromium App-Bound Encryption. Rationale: Article explicitly states: "the PHP payload also extracts a base64-encoded executable, which is written to the %TEMP% folder as a random .exe filename, and then launched." php.exe legitimately almost never spawns .exe children from %TEMP% — combination is article-specific and high-fidelity.
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1140 T1036.005 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php.exe", "php-cgi.exe")
| where FolderPath has @"\AppData\Local\Temp\" or FolderPath has @"\Windows\Temp\"
| where FileName endswith ".exe"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildName   = FileName,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, MD5
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\php.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith @"\php-cgi.exe"
| where NewProcessName has @"\AppData\Local\Temp\" or NewProcessName has @"\Windows\Temp\"
| where NewProcessName endswith ".exe"
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Malicious helpers.php dropped under vendor/laravel-lang/ during Composer install Delivery High
Detects creation of a file named helpers.php under any vendor/laravel-lang/* directory — the exact indicator of the hijacked Laravel Lang packages (lang, http-statuses, attributes, actions). The legitimate packages do not ship a helpers.php under those directories; the malicious one is auto-registered in composer.json's autoload section and acts as the stage-1 dropper. Rationale: Article: "the malicious releases introduced a malicious file named 'src/helpers.php', which was automatically loaded by Composer." The combination of the exact filename + the exact namespace directory (vendor/laravel-lang/) is unique to the four hijacked packages; legitimate Laravel Lang releases prior to compromise did not ship this file. Lookback 60d covers the ~700 historical versions reportedly retagged.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1505.001 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has @"\vendor\laravel-lang\" or FolderPath has "/vendor/laravel-lang/")
| where FileName =~ "helpers.php"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, FileSize,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where (TargetFilePath has @"\vendor\laravel-lang\" or TargetFilePath has "/vendor/laravel-lang/")
| where TargetFileName =~ "helpers.php"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName,
          TargetFileSHA256, TargetFileSize,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Composer command line installing or updating laravel-lang/* packages (scope hunt) Delivery Medium
Hunting query to enumerate every host (dev workstation, CI runner, build agent, container image build) that explicitly invoked Composer to install/update/require any laravel-lang/* package during the compromise window. Used to scope the blast radius of which projects pulled the hijacked tags — pair with UC3 to confirm a malicious helpers.php landed. Rationale: Article names four affected packages (laravel-lang/lang, laravel-lang/http-statuses, laravel-lang/attributes, laravel-lang/actions) and notes ~700 historical versions retagged. The substring 'laravel-lang' on a Composer command line uniquely identifies install/update/require operations targeting any of them. Hunt-tier because composer require/update activity is legitimate on dev hosts — the value is enumeration, not alerting.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1199
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where (FileName =~ "composer" or FileName =~ "composer.phar" or FileName =~ "composer.bat"
         or ProcessCommandLine has "composer.phar"
         or (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "php.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "composer"))
| where ProcessCommandLine has "laravel-lang"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Hits = count(),
            Cmds = make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 25)
            by DeviceName, AccountName
| order by LastSeen desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where (TargetProcessName endswith "composer" or TargetProcessName endswith "composer.phar"
         or TargetProcessCommandLine has "composer.phar"
         or (TargetProcessName endswith "php.exe" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "composer"))
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "laravel-lang"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Hits = count(),
            Cmds = make_set(TargetProcessCommandLine, 25)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername
| order by LastSeen desc

[LLM] Chromium Local State / Login Data accessed by non-browser binary from %TEMP% (App-Bound Encryption theft) Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for a non-browser process — particularly one running from %TEMP% — touching Chrome/Brave/Edge 'Local State' or 'Login Data' files. This is the credential-access behaviour of the DebugElevator binary the Laravel Lang stealer drops on Windows, which extracts App-Bound Encryption keys to decrypt stored browser passwords. Rationale: Article: DebugElevator is "designed to target Chrome, Brave, and Edge, and extract App-Bound Encryption keys needed to decrypt stored browser credentials." The App-Bound Encryption master key lives in the Local State JSON and the encrypted passwords in Login Data — any non-browser binary touching those files, especially one running from %TEMP% under a php.exe parent, is the exact behaviour the article describes. Sigma + Datadog left empty because the detection depends on file-read telemetry that Sigma's file_event category and Sysmon EID 11 (FileCreate) do not natively capture; Falcon FileOpenInfo and Defender DeviceFileEvents (FileCopied/FileRenamed when stealer stages copies) do.
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1539 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)

                            @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\")
   or PreviousFolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\BraveSoftware\Brave-Browser\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\")
| where (FileName in~ ("Local State", "Login Data", "Login Data.tmp", "Cookies", "Web Data"))
     or (PreviousFileName in~ ("Local State", "Login Data", "Cookies", "Web Data"))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe", "msedge.exe", "brave.exe",
                                        "msedgewebview2.exe", "googleupdate.exe",
                                        "microsoftedgeupdate.exe", "elevation_service.exe",

| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\",

   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("php.exe", "php-cgi.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName,

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"

| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.t1555.003

        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'

            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'

level: high

| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine

| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase

    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation

        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'

            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'

falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

[LLM] Packagist supply chain: Composer/npm postinstall fetching parikhpreyash4 GitHub payload Installation High
Detects the article-specific postinstall execution chain where Composer/npm build tooling spawns curl/wget/sh to retrieve the malicious Linux binary from github.com/parikhpreyash4/systemd-network-helper-aa5c751f or stages it to /tmp/.sshd. Targets developer endpoints and CI runners. Rationale: Uses three article-unique strings together — the attacker GitHub handle 'parikhpreyash4', the release asset name 'systemd-network-helper-aa5c751f', and the drop path '/tmp/.sshd'. Any one alone has effectively zero legitimate ground-truth, so cmd-line containment is a clean alerting signal.
ATT&CKT1546.016 T1204.003 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("parikhpreyash4", "systemd-network-helper-aa5c751f", "/tmp/.sshd")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("parikhpreyash4", "systemd-network-helper-aa5c751f", "/tmp/.sshd")
| extend BuildParent = iff(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","npm","npx","yarn","pnpm","composer","composer.phar","php","sh","bash","dash","zsh"), true, false)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, BuildParent
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("parikhpreyash4", "systemd-network-helper-aa5c751f", "/tmp/.sshd")
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("parikhpreyash4", "systemd-network-helper-aa5c751f", "/tmp/.sshd")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Linux dotfile drop at /tmp/.sshd masquerading as OpenSSH daemon Installation High
Detects file creation at the exact /tmp/.sshd path used by the Packagist supply-chain postinstall stager. The dotfile prefix hides the artifact from default `ls`, and the .sshd name impersonates the OpenSSH daemon to blend into Linux process listings. Rationale: Exact path '/tmp/.sshd' is named verbatim in the Socket write-up as the stager's drop location. The dotfile-named-after-sshd pattern is so specific that any hit is high-fidelity; no legitimate Linux package or daemon writes to that exact path.
ATT&CKT1564.001 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FolderPath has "/tmp" and FileName == ".sshd")
   or FolderPath has "/tmp/.sshd"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath =~ "/tmp/.sshd"
   or (TargetFileName == ".sshd" and TargetFilePath has "/tmp")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] gvfsd-network binary executing from non-standard path (GNOME daemon masquerade) Command & Control High
The campaign's second-stage binary is named 'gvfsd-network' to impersonate the legitimate GNOME Virtual File System daemon, which only lives in /usr/libexec or /usr/lib/gvfs. Anything by that name running from /tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm, or user home dirs is the implant. Rationale: Article cites 'The choice of the name "gvfsd-network" for the malware is interesting, as it refers to a GNOME Virtual File System (GVfs) daemon'. The legit binary's install path is fixed by distro packaging, so an allow-list of /usr/libexec + /usr/lib/gvfs is exhaustive — anything else with that name is the implant.
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "gvfsd-network"
| where not (FolderPath startswith "/usr/libexec" or FolderPath startswith "/usr/lib/gvfs" or FolderPath startswith "/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/gvfs")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetProcessName endswith "/gvfsd-network" or TargetProcessName =~ "gvfsd-network"
| where not (TargetProcessName startswith "/usr/libexec/" or TargetProcessName startswith "/usr/lib/gvfs/" or TargetProcessName startswith "/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/gvfs/")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Build tooling spawning curl/wget with TLS verification disabled Installation Medium
The Socket write-up flags TLS-verification bypass as a hide-activity tactic of the malicious postinstall script. Detects curl/wget invocations with --insecure/-k/--no-check-certificate when the parent is a JS/PHP package manager or shell launched by one, which is the article's specific install-time payload chain. Rationale: Article calls out 'disabling TLS verification' as a hide-activity tactic of the postinstall stager. Combining curl/wget + insecure flag + a package-manager parent is article-specific — legit npm/composer post-install scripts pulling assets over HTTPS without verification is itself a red flag worth alerting on.
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ ("curl","wget")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--insecure", " -k ", "--no-check-certificate")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","npm","npx","yarn","pnpm","composer","composer.phar","php","sh","bash","dash","zsh")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where TargetProcessName endswith "/curl" or TargetProcessName endswith "/wget"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("--insecure", " -k ", "--no-check-certificate")
| where ActingProcessName endswith_cs "node" or ActingProcessName endswith_cs "npm" or ActingProcessName endswith_cs "yarn" or ActingProcessName endswith_cs "pnpm" or ActingProcessName endswith_cs "composer" or ActingProcessName endswith_cs "composer.phar" or ActingProcessName endswith_cs "php" or ActingProcessName endswith_cs "sh" or ActingProcessName endswith_cs "bash"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Compromised Packagist Composer package vendor/ presence on hosts Delivery High
Hunting query that surfaces hosts (developer endpoints, CI runners) where any of the 8 trojanized Composer packages was installed under vendor/. Composer drops package files at vendor/<vendor>/<package>/, so a file write to those exact paths is a strong inventory signal regardless of whether the postinstall fired. Rationale: Eight package names are listed verbatim in the article. Composer's deterministic vendor/<owner>/<name>/ install layout means a file write to one of those paths is direct evidence of installation, even if the postinstall script was blocked or already removed by the time of triage.

[LLM] Laravel-Lang supply chain C2/exfil to flipboxstudio.info Command & Control High
Hunts DNS lookups, SNI, or HTTP host headers to flipboxstudio[.]info — the C2/exfil domain used by the May 2026 Laravel-Lang Composer package compromise. The domain hosts both /payload (second-stage) and /exfil (stolen secrets), so any traffic to it from a Laravel-running host or CI runner indicates active compromise. Rationale: flipboxstudio[.]info is the single attacker-controlled C2/exfil endpoint named in the Snyk advisory and corroborated by StepSecurity, The Hacker News, Socket and Cyberpress. The domain has no legitimate use, so any successful resolution or connection is high-fidelity. Hits both DNS and HTTP/SNI telemetry to catch the resolution even if the payload connection is blocked. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-attack • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/laravel-lang-php-packages-compromised.html • https://socket.dev/blog/laravel-lang-compromise • https://github.com/Laravel-Lang/http-statuses/issues/277
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1195.002

[LLM] Laravel-Lang stealer file drop in .laravel_locale temp directory Installation High
Hunts file creation under any .laravel_locale subdirectory of a temp path. The Snyk advisory documents three artifacts under <tmp>/.laravel_locale/: an md5-hashed infection marker, a 12-hex-char .php second-stage stealer, and (on Windows) an 8-hex-char .vbs launcher. The directory name is unique to this campaign and has no benign use. Rationale: The Snyk IOC table explicitly names <tmp>/.laravel_locale/<md5>, <tmp>/.laravel_locale/<12 hex>.php, and <tmp>/.laravel_locale/<8 hex>.vbs as stealer artifacts; StepSecurity corroborates the /tmp staging behaviour. The directory string is unique to this campaign and matches regardless of whether tmp resolves to /tmp, $TMPDIR, or %TEMP%. The filename regex extensions tag which stage fired for fast triage. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-attack • https://socket.dev/blog/laravel-lang-compromise
ATT&CKT1059 T1105 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has ".laravel_locale"
| extend Marker = iff(FileName matches regex @"^[a-f0-9]{32}$", "infection_marker", "")
| extend Stage2 = iff(FileName matches regex @"^[a-f0-9]{12}\.php$", "stealer_php", "")
| extend VbsLauncher = iff(FileName matches regex @"^[a-f0-9]{8}\.vbs$", "vbs_launcher", "")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, Marker, Stage2, VbsLauncher, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has ".laravel_locale"
| extend Marker = iff(TargetFileName matches regex @"^[a-f0-9]{32}$", "infection_marker", "")
| extend Stage2 = iff(TargetFileName matches regex @"^[a-f0-9]{12}\.php$", "stealer_php", "")
| extend VbsLauncher = iff(TargetFileName matches regex @"^[a-f0-9]{8}\.vbs$", "vbs_launcher", "")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, Marker, Stage2, VbsLauncher
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] DebugChromium.exe execution (Laravel-Lang stealer Windows artifact) Installation High
Hunts execution of DebugChromium.exe anywhere on disk. The Snyk advisory names this binary as a Windows artifact observed on hosts infected by the Laravel-Lang Composer supply-chain stealer. The name impersonates a Chrome debug build to blend in with developer tooling; there is no legitimate Microsoft/Google binary by this name. Rationale: DebugChromium.exe is called out by name in the Snyk IOC table as a Windows artifact observed on infected hosts. The string is unique - no legitimate Microsoft or Google product ships a binary by this name - so a process-create on this filename is essentially confirmation of infection. Captures parent (likely cscript.exe from UC4) for chain reconstruction. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-advisory/ • https://securityonline.info/laravel-lang-supply-chain-attack-rce-backdoor/

| where EventID == 4688

[LLM] cscript/wscript executing a script from .laravel_locale temp directory Installation High
Hunts cscript.exe or wscript.exe invocations whose command line references a .laravel_locale path. The Snyk advisory describes the Windows execution chain as the malicious PHP helper writing an 8-hex-char .vbs into %TEMP%\.laravel_locale\ and launching it via cscript — pairing the canonical script interpreter with the stealer's unique staging directory yields a tight signal. Rationale: Snyk explicitly documents the Windows execution chain as a .vbs launcher under %TEMP%\.laravel_locale\. The compound (cscript|wscript) + .laravel_locale leaves no realistic benign matches — neither Windows nor any common dev tool stages scripts in a directory of that name. Captures parent process so triage shows the PHP runtime (php.exe / php-cgi) that originated the launch. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-attack • https://snyk.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-advisory/

[LLM] Compromised laravel-lang Composer package: helpers.php in vendor tree Delivery High
Hunts the file write or presence of src/helpers.php under vendor/laravel-lang/{lang,http-statuses,attributes,actions}/. A legitimate localization package has no reason to ship an autoload-files helper, so any host whose Composer cache contains this file pulled a poisoned tag during the May 22-23 2026 incident and should be treated as compromised until the package is rolled back and credentials rotated. Rationale: The Snyk detection guidance explicitly tells defenders to inspect vendor/laravel-lang/*/ for the presence of src/helpers.php — legitimate releases of these four localization packages do not ship a helpers file or use autoload.files. The package-name regex narrows to the four named-compromised packages (lang, http-statuses, attributes, actions) per the affected-versions table, avoiding stray matches on other laravel-lang/* repos. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/Laravel-Lang/http-statuses/issues/277 • https://gbhackers.com/compromise-laravel-lang-packages/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-attack
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has "vendor\\laravel-lang\\" or FolderPath has "vendor/laravel-lang/"
| where FileName =~ "helpers.php"
| extend Package = extract(@"laravel-lang[\\/](lang|http-statuses|attributes|actions)", 1, FolderPath)
| where isnotempty(Package)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, Package, SHA256, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)

| where TargetFileName =~ "helpers.php"
| extend Package = extract(@"laravel-lang[\\/](lang|http-statuses|attributes|actions)", 1, TargetFilePath)
| where isnotempty(Package)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, Package, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375") or SHA1 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375") or MD5 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375") or SHA1 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375") or MD5 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] PHP/web-server process beaconing to flipboxstudio.info · Network connections to article IPs / domains

[LLM] PHP/web-server process beaconing to flipboxstudio.info Command & Control High
Detects php-fpm, php-cli, or web-server worker processes resolving or connecting to flipboxstudio.info — the first-stage C2 used by the trojanised laravel-lang packages to pull the ~5,900-line PHP stealer. Article-specific because the C2 host is hardcoded into src/helpers.php. Rationale: flipboxstudio.info is the C2 host explicitly named in the article and pre-extracted IOC list; a PHP/web-server worker resolving it during request handling is the textbook auto-loaded helpers.php beacon. Process-context filter keeps FPs near-zero.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "flipboxstudio.info" or RemoteUrl has "flipboxstudio[.]info"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php.exe","php-cgi.exe","php-fpm.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe","php","php-fpm","httpd","nginx","apache2")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let c2 = dynamic(["flipboxstudio.info"]);

[LLM] php-fpm/php-cli spawning cscript.exe with VBS launcher (Laravel-Lang dropper) Installation High
Detects the Windows-specific dropper behaviour of the trojanised laravel-lang helpers.php — a PHP request-handling process spawns cscript.exe to run a VBScript launcher. Article explicitly notes 'delivers a Visual Basic Script launcher on Windows and runs it via cscript.' Rationale: Article literally states 'the dropper delivers a Visual Basic Script launcher on Windows and runs it via cscript.' php.exe → cscript.exe is an extremely rare parent/child pair outside this attack chain; pairing with .vbs argument makes it almost FP-free.
ATT&CKT1059.005 T1059.004 T1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php.exe","php-cgi.exe","php-fpm.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe")
| where FileName =~ "cscript.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has ".vbs" or ProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", "/tmp/")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("php.exe","php-cgi.exe","php-fpm.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\cscript.exe"
| where CommandLine has ".vbs"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine

[LLM] Mass credential-file fan-out reads from single PHP/www-data process Actions on Objectives High
Detects a single PHP/web-server worker process touching multiple high-value credential files within seconds — the fan-out signature of the ~5,900-line laravel-lang stealer's 15 collector modules (AWS, SSH, Kube, .env, wp-config, .git-credentials, browser vaults). Rationale: Article lists 15 specialist collector modules targeting AWS/SSH/Kube/.env/wp-config/.git-credentials/browser Login Data/wallets/password managers — a single PHP worker reading ≥5 of these within 5 minutes is the unmistakable stealer fan-out shape and would never happen during normal request handling. Verbatim path strings (@"\.aws\credentials") avoid the prior KQL escape failure.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555.005 T1539
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let credPaths = dynamic([@"\.aws\credentials", @"\.aws\config", @"\.ssh\id_", @"\.kube\config", @"\.config\gcloud", @"\.git-credentials", @"\.netrc", @"\.gitconfig", "wp-config.php", "docker-compose.yml", ".env", "Login Data", "Cookies", "key3.db", "key4.db", "logins.json", "signons.sqlite", "NordPass", "Bitwarden", "1Password", "LastPass", "KeePass", "electrum", "exodus", "Ledger Live"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed") or ActionType startswith "File"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php.exe","php-cgi.exe","php-fpm.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe","php","php-fpm","httpd","nginx","apache2")
| where FolderPath has_any (credPaths) or FileName has_any (credPaths)
| summarize FileCount = dcount(strcat(FolderPath, FileName)),
            Files = make_set(strcat(FolderPath, FileName), 30),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
  by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where FileCount >= 5
| extend SpanSeconds = datetime_diff('second', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| where SpanSeconds <= 300
| order by LastSeen desc

[LLM] AES-encrypted exfil POST to flipboxstudio.info/exfil Actions on Objectives High
Targets the second-stage exfil channel — HTTP POST from a PHP/web-server worker to flipboxstudio.info/exfil carrying AES-256 encrypted collected credentials. Article explicitly: 'encrypts the results with AES-256 and sends them to flipboxstudio[.]info/exfil.' Rationale: Article gives the exact exfil URL pattern 'flipboxstudio[.]info/exfil' — combining the host, /exfil path, and POST method from a PHP worker is essentially a deterministic IOC match.

)

[LLM] PHP/web-server worker querying cloud metadata IMDS endpoints Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects php-fpm/httpd/nginx/w3wp processes connecting to 169.254.169.254 (AWS/Azure IMDS) or metadata.google.internal — used by the laravel-lang stealer to grab IAM roles, instance identity documents, and GCP/Azure access tokens during the discovery+credential-access phases. Rationale: Article specifies the stealer 'queries cloud metadata endpoints' for IAM roles, GCP application default creds, and Azure access tokens. PHP request-handling processes calling IMDS is non-existent in normal web traffic — at most one app per fleet does this, easy to allowlist.

DeviceNetworkEvents

| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php.exe","php-cgi.exe","php-fpm.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe","php","php-fpm","httpd","nginx","apache2")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
(union isfuzzy=true
  (DnsEvents | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) | where Name has "metadata.google.internal" | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType),

)

[LLM] helpers.php write under vendor/laravel-lang and composer autoload tampering Installation High
File-integrity detection for the persistence vector — src/helpers.php inside vendor/laravel-lang/* being created or modified, or vendor/composer/autoload_files.php being rewritten to reference it. Article confirms 'this file is registered in the composer.json under autoload.files' so the backdoor re-runs every PHP request. Rationale: Article quote: 'this file [src/helpers.php] is registered in the composer.json under autoload.files, the backdoor is executed automatically on every PHP request.' Watching writes to vendor/laravel-lang/*/helpers.php and autoload_files.php is the cleanest persistence detection because it's filesystem-deterministic, language-agnostic across Windows/Linux, and surfaces affected hosts even if C2 is sinkholed.
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has "vendor" and FolderPath has "laravel-lang" and FileName =~ "helpers.php")
   or (FolderPath has "vendor" and FolderPath has "composer" and FileName =~ "autoload_files.php")
   or (FileName =~ "composer.lock")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","FileCreate","FileWrite")
| where (TargetFilePath has "vendor" and TargetFilePath has "laravel-lang" and TargetFileName =~ "helpers.php")
   or (TargetFilePath has "vendor/composer" and TargetFileName =~ "autoload_files.php")
   or TargetFileName =~ "composer.lock"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access

        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'

    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:

author: Clankerusecase

            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'

level: medium

Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("flipboxstudio.info")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["flipboxstudio.info"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

[LLM] LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin CVE-2026-48172 — redisAble exploit request in HTTP/access logs Exploitation High
Hunts the exact LiteSpeed-provided IOC: HTTP requests carrying the cPanel JSON-API parameter cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble against the user-end LiteSpeed plugin. Any successful 2xx hit on this parameter against a server running plugin 2.3–2.4.4 is post-exploitation evidence and should be treated as a confirmed root-level compromise candidate. Rationale: Anchored on the exact vendor-supplied grep IOC from the LiteSpeed advisory (cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble) — a string that has zero legitimate use case in normal cPanel traffic outside this exploitation path. Cross-checked against the GitHub Advisory (GHSA-fxrh-cwjh-m33v), NVD entry, and cybersecuritynews.com / systemtek.co.uk write-ups; all four corroborate the same IOC and affected version range 2.3–2.4.4. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fxrh-cwjh-m33v • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-48172 • https://cybersecuritynews.com/litespeed-cpanel-plugin-0-day-exploited/ • https://www.systemtek.co.uk/2026/05/litespeed-user-end-cpanel-plugin-privilege-escalation-vulnerability-cve-2026-48172/
ATT&CKT1190 T1068
Data sourcesWeb.Web
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble" or AdditionalFields has "cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
let ioc = "cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble";
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestURL has ioc or Message has ioc
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceTable="CommonSecurityLog", DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, DestinationHostName=coalesce(DestinationHostName, DeviceExternalID), RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceAction),
(Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where ProcessName in~ ("httpd","apache2","lsws","cpanellogd","cpsrvd","litespeed") or Facility in~ ("local6","daemon")
  | where SyslogMessage has ioc
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceTable="Syslog", DeviceVendor="cPanel/LiteSpeed", DeviceProduct=ProcessName, SourceIP=extract(@"([0-9]{1,3}(?:\.[0-9]{1,3}){3})", 1, SyslogMessage), DestinationHostName=HostName, RequestURL=SyslogMessage, RequestClientApplication="", DeviceAction=""),
(W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csUriQuery has ioc or csUriStem has ioc
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceTable="W3CIISLog", DeviceVendor="IIS", DeviceProduct="web", SourceIP=cIP, DestinationHostName=Computer, RequestURL=strcat(csUriStem,"?",csUriQuery), RequestClientApplication=csUserAgent, DeviceAction=tostring(scStatus))
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin CVE-2026-48172 redisAble Exploit Attempt
id: 8b0f5d4c-2a91-4d3b-9f7e-1d6f4c8b2a91
status: experimental
description: Detects HTTP requests to the LiteSpeed user-end cPanel plugin abusing the lsws.redisAble JSON-API function to execute scripts as root (CVE-2026-48172, CVSS 10.0). Vendor-published IOC.

[LLM] LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin CVE-2026-48172 — root-privileged child spawned by lsws/cpsrvd worker Installation High
Post-exploitation pivot for CVE-2026-48172. Hunts shell, scripting, or LOLBin children executed with effective UID 0 whose parent is the LiteSpeed or cPanel JSON-API worker process (lsws, cpsrvd, lswsctrld, queueprocd). The vuln's outcome is 'arbitrary scripts as root' — this catches the script execution itself even when the upstream HTTP log was rotated or scrubbed. Rationale: Maps the vuln's stated outcome ('execute arbitrary scripts as root' via lsws.redisAble) to its inevitable on-host artefact: a root-uid child of the LiteSpeed/cPanel daemon. The parent-process list (lsws/cpsrvd/queueprocd/lscmctl) comes from the LiteSpeed plugin layout under /usr/local/lsws/ called out in the article's mitigation command and corroborated by the cPanel daemon naming convention documented in cybersecuritynews.com's write-up. Catches the exploit even when WAF/access logs are missing. Cross-checked against: • https://cybersecuritynews.com/litespeed-cpanel-plugin-0-day-exploited/ • https://www.gotekky.com/guides/security/litespeed-user-end-cpanel-plugin-privilege-escalation-2026/ • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fxrh-cwjh-m33v
ATT&CKT1068 T1059.004 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("lsws","lswsctrld","cpsrvd","cpsrvd-ssl","queueprocd","cpanellogd","lscmctl")
| where AccountName =~ "root"
| where FileName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","perl","python","python3","php","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat","chmod","chown","useradd","usermod","crontab","base64","openssl")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("redisAble","/tmp/","/dev/shm/","-c \"","bash -i","/dev/tcp/","chmod +x","curl -fsSL","wget -qO")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ParentImage=InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ChildImage=FolderPath, ChildCmd=ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let parents = dynamic(["lsws","lswsctrld","cpsrvd","cpsrvd-ssl","queueprocd","cpanellogd","lscmctl"]);
let susp_children = dynamic(["bash","sh","dash","zsh","perl","python","python3","php","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat","chmod","chown","useradd","usermod","crontab","base64","openssl"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcOs has "linux"
| where tolower(ParentProcessName) in (parents) or tolower(tostring(split(ParentProcessName, "/")[-1])) in (parents)
| where TargetUsername =~ "root" or ActorUsername =~ "root"
| where tolower(tostring(split(TargetProcessName, "/")[-1])) in (susp_children)
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("redisAble","/tmp/","/dev/shm/","bash -i","/dev/tcp/","chmod +x","curl -fsSL","wget -qO")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc

status: experimental
description: Detects a root-owned shell, scripting interpreter, or download/persistence LOLBin whose parent is a LiteSpeed or cPanel daemon — the expected post-exploit chain for CVE-2026-48172 (lsws.redisAble running scripts as root).
references:

detection:

      - '/lsws'

      - '/cpsrvd-ssl'
      - '/queueprocd'
      - '/cpanellogd'
      - '/lscmctl'
  selection_user:

  selection_child:

      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/perl'

      - '/python3'
      - '/php'

| ParentBaseFileName=/^(lsws|lswsctrld|cpsrvd|cpsrvd-ssl|queueprocd|cpanellogd|lscmctl)$/i

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48172", "CVE-2026-41940")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48172", "CVE-2026-41940")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Laravel-Lang Supply Chain Attack: Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten to Steal CI Secrets

StepSecurity
2026-05-23 9 use cases 2 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

On May 22, 2026, an attacker with push access to the Laravel-Lang GitHub organization rewrote every git tag across multiple popular Composer packages within a single 15 minute window. Anyone running composer update or installing fresh against laravel-lang/http-statuses, laravel-lang/actions, or laravel-lang/attributes now pulls a payload that exfiltrates CI secrets to a typosquatted attacker domain. StepSecurity confirmed end to end exploitation in an isolated runner and has filed security issues in all four repositories.

ATT&CKT1190 T1195.002

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] GitHub bulk git tag force-push by single actor across multiple org repos
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] PHP CLI drops hidden /tmp dropper artefacts (Laravel-Lang autoload payload) · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Laravel-Lang Supply Chain Attack: Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Re
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Egress to typosquatted C2 flipboxstudio.info (Laravel-Lang Composer SC) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Orphaned process (ppid=1) executing from /tmp hidden hex path (post-dropper stage-2)
[LLM] Egress to typosquatted C2 flipboxstudio.info (Laravel-Lang Composer SC) Command & Control High
Hunts DNS or HTTP(S) callbacks to flipboxstudio.info, the attacker-controlled typosquat of the legitimate flipboxstudio.com used as the stage-1 fetch endpoint (/payload) and stage-2 exfiltration sink (/exfil) by the May 2026 Laravel-Lang Composer supply-chain dropper. Single-IOC alerter — exact-domain match, near-zero FP expectation. Rationale: Anchors on the exact attacker-controlled domain `flipboxstudio.info` named verbatim in the IOC block as both the stage-1 GET endpoint (/payload) and stage-2 POST exfil endpoint (/exfil). The domain is a brand-new typosquat of flipboxstudio.com with no legitimate business use — any hit is high-fidelity.

[LLM] PHP CLI drops hidden /tmp dropper artefacts (Laravel-Lang autoload payload) Installation High
Hunts PHP CLI processes (typically from a composer-driven vendor/autoload.php boot) creating files under /tmp/.laravel_locale/<12-hex>.php or /tmp/.<8-hex> matching the exact dropper naming scheme generated by bin2hex(random_bytes(6)) in the malicious src/helpers.php. Combines hidden-path masquerade with the specific php-as-parent shape. Rationale: Anchors on the exact `/tmp/.laravel_locale/<12 hex chars>.php` PHP loader path and `/tmp/.<8 hex chars>` ELF path named in the IOC block, combined with the php-CLI parent shape that follows from `vendor/autoload.php` invoking the malicious helpers.php. The hex-length pattern matches the article's explicit `bin2hex(random_bytes(6))` naming generator.

   or (FolderPath == "/tmp" and FileName matches regex @"^\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}$")
