ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("206.189.27.39") or RemoteUrl has_any ("")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["206.189.27.39"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic([""]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |

    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

logsource:

    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'

    selection_domain:

            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'

falsepositives:

NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

| append

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-33073")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-33073")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2025-33073")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2025-33073")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/

    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows

    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:

            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'

    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465", "b4592cea69699b2c0737d4e19cff7dca17b5baf5a238cd6da950a37e9986f216", "710a9d2653c8bd3689e451778dab9daec0de4c4c75f900788ccf23ef254b122a", "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517", "bdd5da81ac34d9faa2a5118d4ed8f492239734be02146cd24a0e34270a48a455") or SHA1 in~ ("4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465", "b4592cea69699b2c0737d4e19cff7dca17b5baf5a238cd6da950a37e9986f216", "710a9d2653c8bd3689e451778dab9daec0de4c4c75f900788ccf23ef254b122a", "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517", "bdd5da81ac34d9faa2a5118d4ed8f492239734be02146cd24a0e34270a48a455") or MD5 in~ ("4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465", "b4592cea69699b2c0737d4e19cff7dca17b5baf5a238cd6da950a37e9986f216", "710a9d2653c8bd3689e451778dab9daec0de4c4c75f900788ccf23ef254b122a", "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517", "bdd5da81ac34d9faa2a5118d4ed8f492239734be02146cd24a0e34270a48a455")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465", "b4592cea69699b2c0737d4e19cff7dca17b5baf5a238cd6da950a37e9986f216", "710a9d2653c8bd3689e451778dab9daec0de4c4c75f900788ccf23ef254b122a", "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517", "bdd5da81ac34d9faa2a5118d4ed8f492239734be02146cd24a0e34270a48a455") or SHA1 in~ ("4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465", "b4592cea69699b2c0737d4e19cff7dca17b5baf5a238cd6da950a37e9986f216", "710a9d2653c8bd3689e451778dab9daec0de4c4c75f900788ccf23ef254b122a", "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517", "bdd5da81ac34d9faa2a5118d4ed8f492239734be02146cd24a0e34270a48a455") or MD5 in~ ("4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465", "b4592cea69699b2c0737d4e19cff7dca17b5baf5a238cd6da950a37e9986f216", "710a9d2653c8bd3689e451778dab9daec0de4c4c75f900788ccf23ef254b122a", "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517", "bdd5da81ac34d9faa2a5118d4ed8f492239734be02146cd24a0e34270a48a455")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465", "b4592cea69699b2c0737d4e19cff7dca17b5baf5a238cd6da950a37e9986f216", "710a9d2653c8bd3689e451778dab9daec0de4c4c75f900788ccf23ef254b122a", "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517", "bdd5da81ac34d9faa2a5118d4ed8f492239734be02146cd24a0e34270a48a455"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Megalodon: Mass GitHub Actions Secret Exfiltration Across 5,500+ Public Repositories

StepSecurity
2026-05-22 11 use cases 3 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

A forged commit. A workflow file disguised as a routine CI optimization. Within 6 hours, 5,561 GitHub repositories were backdoored. Cloud credentials harvested. SSH keys stolen. OIDC tokens minted and exfiltrated before any runner finished. The attacker never touched your application code, only your pipeline. Most repositories had no idea it happened.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Megalodon backdoor workflow file (SysDiag.yml / Optimize-Build.yml) written to .github/workflows/ · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Megalodon: Mass GitHub Actions Secret Exfiltration Across 5,500+ Public Reposito
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Megalodon CI/CD exfil: outbound HTTPS to C2 216.126.225.129:8443 · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Megalodon harvester: curl POST to C2 /collect endpoint on Linux runner · [LLM] Megalodon harvester: bash secret-grep across workspace (API_KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PRIVATE_KEY|BEGIN RSA) · [LLM] Megalodon harvester: clustered read of ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.kube/config, ~/.npmrc, ~/.docker/config.json in one session · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Megalodon CI/CD exfil: outbound HTTPS to C2 216.126.225.129:8443 Command & Control High
Detects any host (corporate proxy, EDR-monitored endpoint, self-hosted GitHub Actions runner) initiating a connection to the Megalodon campaign C2 server. The IP/port pair is unique to this campaign and any hit is a near-certain compromise indicator across the org. Rationale: Anchors on the article-published C2 IP 216.126.225.129 — a single hard IOC that StepSecurity attributes directly to the Megalodon campaign. The IP/port combo is not associated with any legitimate service in the article and any internal egress is high-fidelity.
ATT&CKT1041 T1567 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP == "216.126.225.129"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where DestinationIP == "216.126.225.129"
   | project TimeGenerated, Vendor=DeviceVendor, SourceIP, SourceHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, DeviceAction),
  (ImNetworkSession

   | project TimeGenerated, Vendor=EventVendor, SourceIP=SrcIpAddr, SourceHostName=SrcHostname, DestinationIP=DstIpAddr, DestinationPort=DstPortNumber, RequestURL=Url, DeviceAction=DvcAction)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Megalodon harvester: curl POST to C2 /collect endpoint on Linux runner Actions on Objectives High
Detects the runtime exfil step of the Megalodon payload — a curl invocation POSTing gzipped credential blob to https://216.126.225.129:8443/collect. Catches both self-hosted runners and any Linux/Windows host re-executing the decoded payload. Rationale: Pivots on the verbatim exfil command in the article — curl POST to https://216.126.225.129:8443/collect with --data-binary. Combining curl binary + IP + /collect path makes a near-zero-FP detection that catches the payload even if the decoded bash is split across multiple invocations.
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1041 T1059.004

| where FileName =~ "curl" or FileName =~ "curl.exe" or FolderPath endswith "/curl"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "216.126.225.129" and ProcessCommandLine has "/collect"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "curl" or ActingProcessName endswith "curl.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "216.126.225.129" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "/collect"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Megalodon harvester: bash secret-grep across workspace (API_KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PRIVATE_KEY|BEGIN RSA) Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the recursive secret-scrape step of the Megalodon payload — `grep -rE "(API_KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD|PRIVATE_KEY|BEGIN RSA)"` walking the CI checkout looking for hardcoded secrets. The literal token list is the article-published payload string. Rationale: All six tokens (API_KEY, SECRET, TOKEN, PASSWORD, PRIVATE_KEY, BEGIN RSA) appear verbatim in the published bash payload's grep regex. Requiring all six together discriminates Megalodon from generic secret-scanners (gitleaks/trufflehog use their own ruleset, not raw greps with this exact token list).
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1083

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate

| where ActingProcessName endswith "grep"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_all ("API_KEY", "SECRET", "TOKEN", "PASSWORD", "PRIVATE_KEY", "BEGIN RSA")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Megalodon backdoor workflow file (SysDiag.yml / Optimize-Build.yml) written to .github/workflows/ Installation High
Detects creation of a workflow file with one of the two campaign-specific filenames inside any .github/workflows/ directory. Catches developer workstations that cloned/pulled a poisoned repository as well as self-hosted runners checking out the malicious tree. Rationale: Both filenames (SysDiag.yml, Optimize-Build.yml) and the `name:` field values SysDiag / Optimize-Build are called out as the two campaign variants in the article and the recommended GitHub code search anchors. The path scope (.github/workflows/) plus exact filename match make this near-zero-FP.

[LLM] Megalodon harvester: clustered read of ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.kube/config, ~/.npmrc, ~/.docker/config.json in one session Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the credential-collection fan-out pattern — a single process tree reading multiple distinct credential stores (SSH private key, kube config, npm token, Docker registry creds) within a one-minute window. Catches Megalodon even if the bash one-liner is split into separate cat invocations and the C2 IP is not yet contactable. Rationale: Anchors directly on the article's decoded payload (Code blocks 2 and 3) — the exact targets cat'd by the Megalodon harvester: /proc/1/environ, ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.kube/config, ~/.npmrc, ~/.docker/config.json. Requiring ≥3 distinct targets from the same parent within 1 minute discriminates from any single legitimate dotfile-reading tool.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1555
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowMin = 1m;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where FileName =~ "cat" or FolderPath endswith "/cat"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/proc/1/environ","/.ssh/id_","/.kube/config","/.npmrc","/.docker/config.json")
| extend Target = case(
    ProcessCommandLine has "/proc/1/environ","pid1_env",
    ProcessCommandLine has "/.ssh/id_","ssh_key",
    ProcessCommandLine has "/.kube/config","kube",
    ProcessCommandLine has "/.npmrc","npm",
    ProcessCommandLine has "/.docker/config.json","docker",
    "")
| summarize
    DistinctTargets = dcount(Target),
    Targets = make_set(Target, 10),
    SampleCmds = make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 10),
    FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
    LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
    by DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, bin(Timestamp, WindowMin)
| where DistinctTargets >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowMin = 1m;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "cat"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/proc/1/environ","/.ssh/id_","/.kube/config","/.npmrc","/.docker/config.json")
| extend Target = case(
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "/proc/1/environ","pid1_env",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "/.ssh/id_","ssh_key",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "/.kube/config","kube",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "/.npmrc","npm",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "/.docker/config.json","docker",
    "")
| summarize
    DistinctTargets = dcount(Target),
    Targets = make_set(Target, 10),
    SampleCmds = make_set(ActingProcessCommandLine, 10),
    FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
    by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where DistinctTargets >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
source:linux.auditd @process.executable.path:*\/cat @process.command_line:(*\/proc\/1\/environ* OR *\/.ssh\/id_* OR *\/.kube\/config* OR *\/.npmrc* OR *\/.docker\/config.json*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/cat$/i CommandLine=/(\/proc\/1\/environ|\/\.ssh\/id_|\/\.kube\/config|\/\.npmrc|\/\.docker\/config\.json)/
| case {
    CommandLine=/\/proc\/1\/environ/ | target := "pid1";
    CommandLine=/\/\.ssh\/id_/ | target := "ssh";
    CommandLine=/\/\.kube\/config/ | target := "kube";
    CommandLine=/\/\.npmrc/ | target := "npm";
    CommandLine=/\/\.docker\/config\.json/ | target := "docker";
  }
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName], function=[count(field=target, distinct=true, as=distinct_targets), collect([target])])
| distinct_targets >= 3
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmds from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=cat (Processes.process="*/proc/1/environ*" OR Processes.process="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Processes.process="*/.kube/config*" OR Processes.process="*/.npmrc*" OR Processes.process="*/.docker/config.json*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_id Processes.parent_process_name _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | eval is_ssh=if(match(mvjoin(cmds,"|"),"/.ssh/id_"),1,0), is_kube=if(match(mvjoin(cmds,"|"),"/.kube/config"),1,0), is_npm=if(match(mvjoin(cmds,"|"),"/.npmrc"),1,0), is_proc=if(match(mvjoin(cmds,"|"),"/proc/1/environ"),1,0), is_docker=if(match(mvjoin(cmds,"|"),"/.docker/config.json"),1,0) | eval distinct_targets=is_ssh+is_kube+is_npm+is_proc+is_docker | where distinct_targets>=3 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmds from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=cat (Processes.process="*/proc/1/environ*" OR Processes.process="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Processes.process="*/.kube/config*" OR Processes.process="*/.npmrc*" OR Processes.process="*/.docker/config.json*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_id Processes.parent_process_name _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | eval is_ssh=if(match(mvjoin(cmds,"|"),"/.ssh/id_"),1,0), is_kube=if(match(mvjoin(cmds,"|"),"/.kube/config"),1,0), is_npm=if(match(mvjoin(cmds,"|"),"/.npmrc"),1,0), is_proc=if(match(mvjoin(cmds,"|"),"/proc/1/environ"),1,0), is_docker=if(match(mvjoin(cmds,"|"),"/.docker/config.json"),1,0) | eval distinct_targets=is_ssh+is_kube+is_npm+is_proc+is_docker | where distinct_targets>=3 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or SHA1 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or MD5 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or SHA1 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or MD5 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

// Article-specific bespoke detection — Megalodon: Mass GitHub Actions Secret Exfiltration Across 5,500+ Public Reposito
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named

DeviceFileEvents

Ghostwriter Targets Ukraine Government Entities with Prometheus Phishing Malware

The Hacker News
2026-05-22 13 use cases 8 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

The Belarus-aligned threat actor known as Ghostwriter (aka UAC-0057 and UNC1151) has been observed using lures related to Prometheus, a Ukrainian online learning platform, to target government organizations in the country. The activity, per the Computer Emergency Response Team of Ukraine (CERT-UA), involves sending phishing emails to government entities using compromised accounts. It's been

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Ghostwriter OYSTERFRESH: wscript.exe executing .js from user Downloads/Temp/Roaming · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Ghostwriter OYSTERBLUES: wscript.exe writing large encrypted blob to HKCU registry
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Ghostwriter OYSTERBLUES C2: wscript.exe HTTP POST exfiltrating host recon to external IP · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Ghostwriter OYSTERFRESH: wscript.exe executing .js from user Downloads/Temp/Roaming Delivery High
Hunts the OYSTERFRESH delivery chain CERT-UA attributes to UAC-0057 (Ghostwriter): victim opens PDF lure, clicks a Prometheus-themed link that downloads a ZIP; extracted .js is executed under wscript.exe from a user-writable path. Pairs the named binary with the unzip-from-Downloads behaviour to keep false positives bounded. Rationale: Uses three article-anchored signals: (1) wscript.exe as the JS runtime CERT-UA names; (2) a user-writable archive-extraction directory because the article specifies ZIP→JS unzip; (3) a parent set restricted to browsers/archivers/mail clients that would have produced the unpack. CERT-UA's mitigation guidance to 'restrict wscript.exe for standard user accounts' confirms this is the load-bearing execution primitive. Cross-checked against: • https://cert.gov.ua/article • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1086/
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1204.002 T1566.002

[LLM] Ghostwriter OYSTERBLUES: wscript.exe writing large encrypted blob to HKCU registry Installation High
Hunts the fileless storage step of OYSTERFRESH: after first execution, the stager writes the obfuscated/encrypted OYSTERBLUES payload into a HKCU registry value (rather than disk) so OYSTERSHUCK can later decode it. Pairs wscript.exe as the writing process with a HKCU\Software target and a payload-sized value (>4 KB) — neither alone is suspicious, the combination is. Rationale: Three article-derived constraints stack: wscript.exe (the named runtime), HKCU\Software (the article says the encrypted blob is written to the registry; HKCU\Software is the only writable hive for a standard user where this fits), and value length >4 KB (encrypted payload large enough to hold a Cobalt Strike loader cannot fit in a Run-key-sized string). Falcon left empty because the listed FDR schema reference only exposes AsepValueUpdate (autostart entries), and OYSTERBLUES does not necessarily land in an autostart key — the generic registry-value write event is outside the documented schema. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/011/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1086/
ATT&CKT1112 T1027.011 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "wscript.exe"
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has @"HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software"
| extend ValueLen = strlen(tostring(RegistryValueData))
| where ValueLen > 4096
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueType, ValueLen
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "wscript.exe"
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software", @"HKCU\Software")
| extend ValueLen = strlen(tostring(RegistryValueData))
| where ValueLen > 4096
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueType, ValueLen
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Ghostwriter OYSTERBLUES C2: wscript.exe HTTP POST exfiltrating host recon to external IP Command & Control High
Hunts the OYSTERBLUES C2 beacon CERT-UA describes: wscript.exe running the OYSTERBLUES JS makes an HTTP POST to an attacker server carrying computer name, user, OS version, last-boot time and running-process list, then eval()s the JS response (which lands Cobalt Strike). Detection is wscript.exe as the network-initiating process to a public IP on HTTP(S) ports. Rationale: Anchored on the article's two explicit C2 facts: (1) the beacon is wscript.exe (CERT-UA names it as the runtime and recommends restricting it), and (2) the channel is an HTTP POST to a C2 server (so HTTP(S) ports + public IP). wscript.exe legitimately almost never reaches the public internet — that single combination is highly specific. Sentinel query rebuilt as ImProcessCreate-to-ImNetworkSession join because ImNetworkSession has no process-name column. Cross-checked against: • https://cert.gov.ua/article • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1059.007 T1041 T1082
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "wscript.exe"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where RemotePort in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let WindowMinutes = 30m;
let WscriptProcs = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName endswith "wscript.exe"
    | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
    | project ProcTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessId;
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where NetworkDirection == "Outbound"
| where DstPortNumber in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| where not(ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr))
| join kind=inner WscriptProcs on DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated between (ProcTime .. (ProcTime + WindowMinutes))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessCommandLine, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkBytes
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @Image:(*\\wscript.exe OR *\\WScript.exe OR *\\WSCRIPT.EXE) @DestinationPort:(80 OR 443 OR 8080 OR 8443) NOT CIDR(@DestinationIp, 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.0.0/16, 172.16.0.0/12, 127.0.0.0/8)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ContextImageFileName=/\\wscript\.exe$/i
| RemotePort=80 OR RemotePort=443 OR RemotePort=8080 OR RemotePort=8443
| NOT cidr("10.0.0.0/8", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("192.168.0.0/16", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("172.16.0.0/12", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("127.0.0.0/8", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=count())

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web

| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

| rename All_Email.recipient as user

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count

        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email

     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`

     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")

| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

[LLM] YesWiki Bazar form-import volumetric POST — CVE-2026-46670 blind SQLi extraction loop Exploitation High
Hunts the byte-by-byte extraction loop used to exploit CVE-2026-46670 in YesWiki. The PoC drives one POST to /?BazaR&vue=formulaire per character of the hex-encoded value being exfiltrated from yeswiki_users, producing dozens-to-hundreds of POSTs to a single URI from a single source IP in a short window — an unusual pattern for a wiki application. Rationale: Locks on the article's exact request shape (POST + csUriQuery containing both 'BazaR' and 'vue=formulaire') and the unavoidable property of the PoC: blind extraction requires N requests for N characters of the password hash, so a per-source-IP POST count >=20 in 5 min to this single endpoint is a strong signal that something other than a human is wiki-ing. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jwvv-qr7q-cv8j • https://github.com/YesWiki/yeswiki/blob/1f485c049db030b94c047ec219e63534ac81142e/tools/bazar/services/FormManager.php#L258
ATT&CKT1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb
let WindowMinutes = 5m;
let PostThreshold = 20;
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod =~ "POST"

[LLM] Non-browser User-Agent against YesWiki Bazar form-import endpoint — CVE-2026-46670 exploit tooling Exploitation High
Hunts the PoC's exploit fingerprint: a request to /?BazaR&vue=formulaire from a scripting-language User-Agent (the published PoC uses Python-urllib/3.13). Real users post Bazar forms from a browser; a curl/python/PowerShell UA on this exact endpoint is high-signal for CVE-2026-46670 exploitation or reconnaissance. Rationale: The published PoC literally ships with User-Agent: Python-urllib/3.13 (from the Burp capture in the article body). The Bazar form-import endpoint is a low-traffic admin path on YesWiki; a scripting-language UA hitting it via POST is rarely benign and matches both the public PoC and copycat exploitation. Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory at github.com/advisories/GHSA-jwvv-qr7q-cv8j. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jwvv-qr7q-cv8j

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] CVE-2026-34926 Trend Micro Apex One On-Premise Server fleet exposure surveillance
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Trend Micro Apex One agent service spawning LOLBin/script-interpreter children (CVE-2026-34926 post-exploit fleet-poisoning symptom)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] CVE-2026-34926 Trend Micro Apex One On-Premise Server fleet exposure surveillance Exploitation High
Inventory all Windows hosts in TVM/vulnerability data reporting exposure to CVE-2026-34926 (Apex One on-premise directory traversal). Because exploitation requires admin access to the Apex One server and TrendAI has already observed in-the-wild attempts, every unpatched server is on a 14-day federal CISA KEV clock (deadline 2026-06-04). The detection isn't behavioural — it's a posture pivot that tells the SOC exactly which servers to wrap with the behavioural UC below until they're patched to SP1 CP Build 18012 or SP1 Build 17079. Rationale: The CVE ID itself (CVE-2026-34926) is the highest-fidelity string in the article — it maps cleanly to a single row in vulnerability inventory tables. Cross-checked vendor bulletin KA-0023430 for fixed builds (SP1 CP Build 18012 / SP1 Build 17079) and CISA KEV catalog for the 2026-06-04 federal remediation deadline, both confirming the CVE is in-scope. Cross-checked against: • https://success.trendmicro.com/en-US/solution/KA-0023430 • https://www.securityweek.com/trendai-patches-apex-one-zero-day-exploited-in-the-wild/ • https://www.jpcert.or.jp/english/at/2026/at260014.html • https://www.hkcert.org/security-bulletin/trend-micro-apex-one-multiple-vulnerabilities_20260522

[LLM] Trend Micro Apex One agent service spawning LOLBin/script-interpreter children (CVE-2026-34926 post-exploit fleet-poisoning symptom) Installation Medium
The article specifically describes the exploitation outcome as 'inject malicious code to deploy to agents on affected installations' — i.e. the Apex One server pushes attacker-controlled code which executes under the agent service context on every managed endpoint. This hunt targets the symptom on the agent fleet: Apex One agent service binaries (PccNTMon.exe, TmListen.exe, NTRtScan.exe, TmCCSF.exe, OfcDog.exe and the Trend service-host family) spawning interpreters / LOLBins that the agent has no legitimate reason to invoke. Scope tightly to the disclosure window (2026-05-21 onward) and to fleets managed by any unpatched on-prem Apex One server surfaced by UC#1. Rationale: Anchored to the article's explicit exploitation outcome: 'inject malicious code to deploy to agents on affected installations'. The parent-process list (PccNTMon, TmListen, NTRtScan, TmCCSF, etc.) is publicly-documented Apex One agent service inventory from Trend Micro product documentation, and a Trend Micro signed service spawning LOLBins is genuinely anomalous behaviour. Filter on InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName='Trend Micro' confirms we're hitting the real agent and not an impersonator. The 2026-05-21 cutoff bounds the hunt to the disclosure window for CISA KEV (KEV add date). Cross-checked against: • https://success.trendmicro.com/en-US/solution/KA-0023430 • https://www.securityweek.com/trendai-patches-apex-one-zero-day-exploited-in-the-wild/ • https://securityaffairs.com/192529/hacking/u-s-cisa-adds-trend-micro-apex-one-and-langflow-to-its-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog.html

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"

Drupal: Critical SQL injection flaw now targeted in attacks

BleepingComputer
2026-05-22 4 use cases 1 technique 3 kill-chain phases detected

Drupal is warning that hackers are attempting to exploit a "highly critical" SQL injection vulnerability announced earlier this week. [...]

CVEsCVE-2026-9082
ATT&CKT1190

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Unauthenticated SQLi probe against Drupal endpoints (CVE-2026-9082) · [LLM] Drupal/PHP/web server process spawning shell or LOLBin (post-CVE-2026-9082 RCE)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Web server writes PHP/PHAR file outside Drupal's compiled-twig path (webshell drop)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] Unauthenticated SQLi probe against Drupal endpoints (CVE-2026-9082) Exploitation Medium
Hunts inbound HTTP requests that target known Drupal API/render endpoints with PHP array-key injection markers or PostgreSQL-specific SQLi syntax characteristic of CVE-2026-9082 EntityQuery condition handler abuse. Article-specific because the flaw is reached via crafted array keys passed to the database abstraction API, leaving telltale `[...']`, `pg_sleep`, `pg_read_file`, or `COPY ... FROM PROGRAM` tokens in URLs/POST bodies on Drupal paths. Rationale: Anchored on the article-confirmed root cause (PHP array-key injection reaching the PostgreSQL EntityQuery condition handler) and the Searchlight Cyber PoC writeup describing anonymous SQLi via crafted bracket/quote keys; PostgreSQL-only RCE primitives (`COPY ... FROM PROGRAM`, `pg_read_file`, `lo_import`) are unique enough to be high-fidelity if seen in a Drupal URL. Cross-checked against: • https://www.drupal.org/sa-core-2026-004 • https://slcyber.io/research-center/keys-to-the-kingdom-anonymous-sql-injection-in-drupal-core-cve-2026-9082/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/highly-critical-drupal-core-flaw.html • https://www.tenable.com/blog/cve-2026-9082-highly-critical-sql-injection-vulnerability-in-drupal-core-sa-core-2026-004
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let LookbackHours = 24h;
let DrupalPaths = dynamic(["/jsonapi/","/node/","/views/ajax","/search/","/rest/","/entity/","/user/login","/?q="]);
let SqliMarkers = dynamic(["pg_sleep","UNION SELECT","union select","COPY FROM PROGRAM","pg_read_file","lo_import","%5B%27","%27%5D","' OR '","')--","--+"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
    | where csUriStem has_any (DrupalPaths)
    | where (csUriQuery has_any (SqliMarkers)) or (csUriQuery has "[" and csUriQuery has "'")
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=cIP, Host=Computer, Url=strcat(csUriStem,"?",csUriQuery), Method=csMethod, Status=scStatus, UA=csUserAgent, Src="IIS"),
  (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
    | where Url has_any (DrupalPaths)
    | where Url has_any (SqliMarkers) or (Url has "[" and Url has "'")
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, Host=DstHostname, Url, Method=HttpMethod, Status=HttpStatusCode, UA=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, Src="ASIM")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Drupal CVE-2026-9082 SQL Injection Probe
id: 6f3d2a14-2a3e-4ee0-9c4b-7a0d2b8e1101
status: experimental
description: Detects inbound HTTP requests targeting Drupal endpoints with PHP array-key injection or PostgreSQL-specific SQLi markers indicative of CVE-2026-9082 exploitation.
references:
  - https://www.drupal.org/sa-core-2026-004
  - https://slcyber.io/research-center/keys-to-the-kingdom-anonymous-sql-injection-in-drupal-core-cve-2026-9082/
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/drupal-critical-sql-injection-flaw-now-targeted-in-attacks/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection_path:
    cs-uri-stem|contains:
      - '/jsonapi/'
      - '/node/'
      - '/views/ajax'
      - '/search/'
      - '/rest/'
      - '/entity/'
      - '/user/login'
      - '/?q='
  selection_payload:
    cs-uri-query|contains:
      - 'pg_sleep'
      - 'UNION SELECT'
      - 'union select'
      - 'COPY FROM PROGRAM'
      - 'pg_read_file'
      - 'lo_import'
      - "%5B%27"
      - "%27%5D"
      - "')--"
      - "' OR '"
  condition: selection_path and selection_payload
falsepositives:
  - Authorised vulnerability scans (Tenable, Burp, Nuclei)
  - Internal pentest activity
level: high
(source:(nginx OR apache OR nginx.access OR apache.access OR iis)) AND (@http.url_details.path:(*/jsonapi/* OR */node/* OR */views/ajax* OR */search/* OR */rest/* OR */entity/* OR */user/login*)) AND (@http.url:(*pg_sleep* OR *PG_SLEEP* OR *pg_read_file* OR *COPY*FROM*PROGRAM* OR *lo_import* OR *UNION*SELECT* OR *union*select* OR *%5B%27* OR *%27%5D* OR *'* OR *%27*))
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.uri_query) as uri_query values(Web.user_agent) as ua values(Web.http_method) as method from datamodel=Web where (Web.uri_path="*/jsonapi/*" OR Web.uri_path="*/node/*" OR Web.uri_path="*/views/ajax*" OR Web.uri_path="*/search/*" OR Web.uri_path="*/rest/*" OR Web.uri_path="*/entity/*" OR Web.uri_path="*/user/login*" OR Web.uri_path="*/?q=*") AND (Web.url="*pg_sleep*" OR Web.url="*UNION*SELECT*" OR Web.url="*COPY*FROM*PROGRAM*" OR Web.url="*pg_read_file*" OR Web.url="*lo_import*" OR Web.url="*%5B*%27*%5D*" OR Web.url="*[*'*]*" OR Web.url="*--+*" OR Web.url="*%27)*OR*%27*") by Web.dest Web.src Web.uri_path Web.http_method Web.status host | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.uri_query) as uri_query values(Web.user_agent) as ua values(Web.http_method) as method from datamodel=Web where (Web.uri_path="*/jsonapi/*" OR Web.uri_path="*/node/*" OR Web.uri_path="*/views/ajax*" OR Web.uri_path="*/search/*" OR Web.uri_path="*/rest/*" OR Web.uri_path="*/entity/*" OR Web.uri_path="*/user/login*" OR Web.uri_path="*/?q=*") AND (Web.url="*pg_sleep*" OR Web.url="*UNION*SELECT*" OR Web.url="*COPY*FROM*PROGRAM*" OR Web.url="*pg_read_file*" OR Web.url="*lo_import*" OR Web.url="*%5B*%27*%5D*" OR Web.url="*[*'*]*" OR Web.url="*--+*" OR Web.url="*%27)*OR*%27*") by Web.dest Web.src Web.uri_path Web.http_method Web.status host | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] Drupal/PHP/web server process spawning shell or LOLBin (post-CVE-2026-9082 RCE) Exploitation High
Detects classic web-to-shell post-exploitation where php-fpm/apache/nginx/IIS w3wp (the typical Drupal runtimes) parents a shell, LOLBin, or reverse-shell one-liner. This is the highest-fidelity host-side signal that the SQLi described in the article has been escalated to RCE via Drupal's PostgreSQL backend. Rationale: Drupal sites run under php-fpm/apache/nginx/w3wp; the article explicitly states CVE-2026-9082 can yield RCE on PostgreSQL backends. Web-server parent + shell/LOLBin child is the canonical post-RCE pivot — high-confidence even without a specific payload string, because Drupal's runtime almost never legitimately spawns /bin/sh, nc, or PowerShell encoded commands. Cross-checked against Drupal SA-CORE-2026-004 and Searchlight Cyber PoC. Cross-checked against: • https://www.drupal.org/sa-core-2026-004 • https://slcyber.io/research-center/keys-to-the-kingdom-anonymous-sql-injection-in-drupal-core-cve-2026-9082/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/highly-critical-drupal-core-flaw.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WebParents = dynamic(["php-fpm","php-fpm.exe","httpd","httpd.exe","apache2","nginx","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe","php-cgi.exe","php.exe","php","drush"]);
let ShellChildren = dynamic(["sh","bash","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wget","curl","perl","python","python3","nc","ncat","socat","whoami","id","uname","hostname"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (WebParents)
| where FileName in~ (ShellChildren)
    or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/dev/tcp/","bash -i","sh -i","nc -e","mkfifo","python -c","perl -e","-NoProfile -enc","-NoP -e","Invoke-WebRequest","DownloadString","curl http","wget http")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WebParents = dynamic(["php-fpm","php-fpm.exe","httpd","httpd.exe","apache2","nginx","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe","php-cgi.exe","php.exe","php","drush"]);
let ShellChildren = dynamic(["sh","bash","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wget","curl","perl","python","python3","nc","ncat","socat","whoami","id","uname"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| extend ParentBase = tolower(tostring(split(replace_string(ParentProcessName,"\\","/"),"/")[-1]))
| extend ChildBase  = tolower(tostring(split(replace_string(ActingProcessName,"\\","/"),"/")[-1]))
| where ParentBase in (WebParents)
| where ChildBase in (ShellChildren)
    or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/dev/tcp/","bash -i","sh -i","nc -e","mkfifo","python -c","perl -e","-NoProfile -enc","Invoke-WebRequest","DownloadString")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Web server writes PHP/PHAR file outside Drupal's compiled-twig path (webshell drop) Installation High
Detects php-fpm/apache/nginx/IIS w3wp creating .php/.phtml/.phar/.inc files in locations other than Drupal's known compiled-template cache. Article-specific because CVE-2026-9082's RCE primitive on PostgreSQL (via `COPY ... FROM PROGRAM` or PHP write through file-include chains) typically lands as a webshell in the document root or `sites/default/files/`. Rationale: Drupal's only legitimate PHP-write path at runtime is the compiled twig cache under `sites/default/files/php/twig/`; anything else written by the PHP runtime is highly suspect. The article + Drupal SA-CORE-2026-004 confirm RCE is possible on PostgreSQL backends, and webshells in `sites/default/files/` are the textbook post-exploitation artefact for Drupal compromises (consistent with prior Drupalgeddon campaigns). Cross-checked against: • https://www.drupal.org/sa-core-2026-004 • https://slcyber.io/research-center/keys-to-the-kingdom-anonymous-sql-injection-in-drupal-core-cve-2026-9082/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (WebParents)
| where FileName endswith ".php" or FileName endswith ".phtml" or FileName endswith ".phar" or FileName endswith ".inc"
| where not(FolderPath has_any ("files/php/twig","files\\php\\twig","core/lib","core\\lib","/vendor/","\\vendor\\"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, FileSize,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc

| extend ProcBase = tolower(tostring(split(replace_string(ActingProcessName,"\\","/"),"/")[-1]))
