// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-9082")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-9082")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

[LLM] MiniUpdate UpdateChecker.dll sideload via legitimate signed .NET host Installation High
Detects loading of the Screening Serpens MiniUpdate payload (internal name UpdateChecker.dll) by a legitimate signed .NET host process via DLL sideloading. The DLL is dropped alongside a hijack-vulnerable benign binary from the Hiring Portal.zip lure and loaded from non-standard user-writable directories. Rationale: Pivots on Unit 42's named internal DLL `UpdateChecker.dll` plus the eight published SHA256 hashes for the MiniUpdate RAT family. User-writable path filter mirrors Screening Serpens' Hiring Portal.zip ZIP-extract sideload chain. Cross-checked against Check Point's 2025 UNC1549 report and MITRE T1574.014 (AppDomainManager Injection). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1019/ • https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/iranian-cyber-actors-target-europe/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/014/
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1574.014

[LLM] Screening Serpens AppDomainManager hijack via .NET app .config tampering Installation High
Detects writes of a .NET application configuration file (appname.exe.config) containing an `appDomainManagerAssembly` / `appDomainManagerType` entry that redirects CLR initialization to a sideloaded assembly. This is the core Screening Serpens 2026 evolution that disables target app security and loads MiniUpdate/MiniJunk V2 RATs. Rationale: Targets the specific Unit 42-described evolution: AppDomainManager hijacking that manipulates .NET initialization via a legitimate .config file. The pattern of a same-directory triple (legitimate signed EXE + attacker EXE.config + attacker DLL) in user-writable paths is highly specific to this campaign and rarely seen in legitimate software, which always installs to Program Files via MSI/trusted installers. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/014/ • https://pentestlab.blog/2020/05/20/persistence-appdomainmanager/ • https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/iranian-cyber-actors-target-europe/
ATT&CKT1574.014 T1574.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName endswith ".exe.config"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Users\", @"\AppData\", @"\Temp\", @"\Downloads\", @"\ProgramData\")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msiexec.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe","wusa.exe","setup.exe","installer.exe","OfficeClickToRun.exe","GoogleUpdate.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files (x86)"
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName endswith ".dll"
    | where FolderPath has_any (@"\Users\", @"\AppData\", @"\Temp\", @"\Downloads\", @"\ProgramData\")
    | project DllTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DllFolder=FolderPath, DllName=FileName, DllSHA256=SHA256, DllWriter=InitiatingProcessFileName
) on DeviceId
| where abs(datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, DllTime)) < 300 and tolower(FolderPath) == tolower(DllFolder)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, ConfigPath=FolderPath, ConfigName=FileName, DllName, DllSHA256, DllWriter, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let configWrites = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName endswith ".exe.config"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Users\", @"\AppData\", @"\Temp\", @"\Downloads\", @"\ProgramData\")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("msiexec.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe","wusa.exe","setup.exe","OfficeClickToRun.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ConfigPath=TargetFilePath, ConfigName=TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine;
let dllWrites = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName endswith ".dll"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Users\", @"\AppData\", @"\Temp\", @"\Downloads\", @"\ProgramData\")
| project DllTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DllPath=TargetFilePath, DllName=TargetFileName, DllSHA256=TargetFileSHA256;
configWrites
| join kind=inner dllWrites on DvcHostname
| where abs(datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, DllTime)) < 300
| extend ConfigDir = substring(ConfigPath, 0, strlen(ConfigPath) - strlen(ConfigName))
| extend DllDir = substring(DllPath, 0, strlen(DllPath) - strlen(DllName))
| where tolower(ConfigDir) == tolower(DllDir)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ConfigPath, ConfigName, DllName, DllSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*.exe.config OR *.EXE.config OR *.exe.CONFIG)) (@TargetFilename:(*\\Users\\* OR *\\AppData\\* OR *\\Temp\\* OR *\\Downloads\\* OR *\\ProgramData\\*)) -@Image:(*\\msiexec.exe OR *\\MsiExec.exe OR *\\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\\OfficeClickToRun.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\.exe\.config$/i
| TargetFileName=/\\(Users|AppData|Temp|Downloads|ProgramData)\\/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(msiexec|TrustedInstaller|OfficeClickToRun|GoogleUpdate|wusa|setup)\.exe$/i
| join({#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\.dll$/i | TargetFileName=/\\(Users|AppData|Temp|Downloads|ProgramData)\\/i}, field=aid, key=DllAid, include=[TargetFileName, SHA256HashData, _time])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())

[LLM] Screening Serpens C2 — DNS/network to UNC1549 infrastructure (Feb-Apr 2026) Command & Control High
Detects any DNS resolution or network connection to the four Unit 42-published Screening Serpens C2 domains used during the Feb-Apr 2026 espionage campaign against US, Israel, UAE and Middle Eastern targets. These domains are dedicated per-target/per-variant and seeing any single resolution is high-fidelity. Rationale: All four domains are explicitly named in the Unit 42 article as Screening Serpens C2 infrastructure for the Feb-Apr 2026 MiniUpdate/MiniJunk V2 campaign. The note `buisness-centeral-transportation.com` (deliberate typosquat of `business-central-transportation`) and `ramiltonsfinance.com` are highly unusual lures unlikely to appear in benign traffic. Cross-checked against MITRE G1019 (UNC1549) and Check Point's earlier Western Europe expansion report. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1019/ • https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/iranian-cyber-actors-target-europe/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004 T1583.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
let c2Domains = dynamic(["business-startup.org","buisness-centeral-transportation.com","premierhealthadvisory.com","ramiltonsfinance.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (c2Domains) or RemoteUrl endswith ".business-startup.org" or RemoteUrl endswith ".buisness-centeral-transportation.com" or RemoteUrl endswith ".premierhealthadvisory.com" or RemoteUrl endswith ".ramiltonsfinance.com"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let c2Domains = dynamic(["business-startup.org","buisness-centeral-transportation.com","premierhealthadvisory.com","ramiltonsfinance.com"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where Name has_any (c2Domains)
| project TimeGenerated, Source="DnsEvents", Host=Computer, SrcIp=ClientIP, Query=Name, RemoteIp=tostring(IPAddresses)),
(ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where DnsQuery has_any (c2Domains)
| project TimeGenerated, Source="ImDnsActivity", Host=SrcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, Query=DnsQuery, RemoteIp=tostring(DnsResponseName)),
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where DestinationHostName has_any (c2Domains) or DestinationDnsDomain has_any (c2Domains) or RequestURL has_any (c2Domains)
| project TimeGenerated, Source="CommonSecurityLog", Host=SourceHostName, SrcIp=SourceIP, Query=coalesce(DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain, RequestURL), RemoteIp=DestinationIP),
(ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where Url has_any (c2Domains) or HttpHostName has_any (c2Domains)
| project TimeGenerated, Source="ImWebSession", Host=SrcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, Query=coalesce(HttpHostName, Url), RemoteIp=DstIpAddr)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Screening Serpens C2 Domain Resolution
id: 9e2a8b41-7d3c-4f6e-aa28-3b7c9d1e4f85
description: Detects DNS/HTTP traffic to Iranian APT Screening Serpens (UNC1549) C2 domains observed during the Feb-Apr 2026 MiniUpdate/MiniJunk V2 campaign documented by Unit 42.
references:

  condition: selection
level: critical
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:windows.security OR source:zeek OR source:cisco-umbrella OR source:cloudflare) (@dns.question.name:(*business-startup.org OR *buisness-centeral-transportation.com OR *premierhealthadvisory.com OR *ramiltonsfinance.com) OR @network.destination.domain:(*business-startup.org OR *buisness-centeral-transportation.com OR *premierhealthadvisory.com OR *ramiltonsfinance.com) OR @http.url:(*business-startup.org* OR *buisness-centeral-transportation.com* OR *premierhealthadvisory.com* OR *ramiltonsfinance.com*) OR @QueryName:(*business-startup.org OR *buisness-centeral-transportation.com OR *premierhealthadvisory.com OR *ramiltonsfinance.com))
(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest OR #event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 OR #event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP6)
| (DomainName=/(^|\.)(business-startup\.org|buisness-centeral-transportation\.com|premierhealthadvisory\.com|ramiltonsfinance\.com)$/i)

[LLM] Screening Serpens recruitment lure — Hiring Portal.zip + job requisition PDFs Delivery High
Detects delivery of the Screening Serpens spear-phishing lure: an archive named Hiring Portal.zip (or nested within an outer ZIP) accompanied by job-requisition PDFs following the pattern '*Software Engineer*Job ID JR######*.pdf'. Targets technical personnel in aerospace, defense and telecom sectors. Rationale: Pivots on the specific lure filename `Hiring Portal.zip` named by Unit 42 (and previously by Check Point research as a Screening Serpens artifact), plus the documented job-requisition PDF pattern (e.g., `Senior Software Engineer Job ID JR205894.pdf`). Restricting to user-download locations cuts the FP rate from generic HR keyword matches on email gateways. Cross-checked against: • https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/iranian-cyber-actors-target-europe/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1019/
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002 T1036.005
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Filesystem
let lureFileNames = dynamic(["Hiring Portal.zip","Hiring_Portal.zip","HiringPortal.zip"]);
let email = EmailAttachmentInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where FileName in~ (lureFileNames) or FileName matches regex @"(?i)^.*Software Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$" or FileName matches regex @"(?i)^.*Senior.*Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$"
| join kind=leftouter (EmailEvents | project NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation) on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, FileName, FileType, SHA256, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation;
let host = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where (FileName in~ (lureFileNames)) or (FileName matches regex @"(?i)^.*(Software|Senior|Principal).*Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Desktop\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, FileOriginUrl;
union email, host
| order by Timestamp desc
let lureFileNames = dynamic(["Hiring Portal.zip","Hiring_Portal.zip","HiringPortal.zip"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where TargetFileName in~ (lureFileNames) or TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)^.*(Software|Senior|Principal).*Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Desktop\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Screening Serpens Hiring Portal Lure Archive
id: 4b8c2e15-d6f3-4e1a-9a7c-5e2f8b3d917a
description: Detects creation of the Hiring Portal.zip archive used as the Screening Serpens (UNC1549) MiniUpdate/MiniJunk V2 spear-phishing lure (Unit 42, May 2026).
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/tracking-iran-apt-screening-serpens/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.t1566.001
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_archive:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\Hiring Portal.zip'
      - '\Hiring_Portal.zip'
      - '\HiringPortal.zip'
  selection_pdf:
    TargetFilename|re: '(?i).*(Software|Senior|Principal).*Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$'
  user_paths:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\Downloads\'
      - '\Desktop\'
      - '\Temp\'
  condition: (selection_archive or selection_pdf) and user_paths
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR email.proofpoint OR email.mimecast OR office365) (@TargetFilename:(*\\Hiring\ Portal.zip OR *\\Hiring_Portal.zip OR *\\HiringPortal.zip) OR @attachment.filename:("Hiring Portal.zip" OR Hiring_Portal.zip OR HiringPortal.zip) OR @email.subject:(*Hiring\ Portal* OR *Job\ Requisition* OR *JR205894*) OR @TargetFilename:(*Software\ Engineer*Job\ ID\ JR* OR *Senior*Engineer*Job\ ID\ JR*))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| (TargetFileName=/\\Hiring[\s_]?Portal\.zip$/i OR TargetFileName=/(Software|Senior|Principal).*Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$/i)
| TargetFileName=/\\(Downloads|Desktop|Temp)\\/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Email.src_user) as sender values(All_Email.recipient) as recipient values(All_Email.subject) as subject from datamodel=Email.All_Email where All_Email.file_name="Hiring Portal.zip" OR All_Email.file_name="Hiring_Portal.zip" OR All_Email.subject IN ("*Hiring Portal*","*Job Requisition*","*JR2058*") by All_Email.message_id All_Email.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)` | append [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name IN ("Hiring Portal.zip","Hiring_Portal.zip") OR (Filesystem.file_name="*Job ID JR*.pdf" AND Filesystem.file_path="*\\Downloads\\*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Email.src_user) as sender values(All_Email.recipient) as recipient values(All_Email.subject) as subject from datamodel=Email.All_Email where All_Email.file_name="Hiring Portal.zip" OR All_Email.file_name="Hiring_Portal.zip" OR All_Email.subject IN ("*Hiring Portal*","*Job Requisition*","*JR2058*") by All_Email.message_id All_Email.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)` | append [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name IN ("Hiring Portal.zip","Hiring_Portal.zip") OR (Filesystem.file_name="*Job ID JR*.pdf" AND Filesystem.file_path="*\\Downloads\\*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`]
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("business-startup.org", "buisness-centeral-transportation.com", "premierhealthadvisory.com", "ramiltonsfinance.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["business-startup.org", "buisness-centeral-transportation.com", "premierhealthadvisory.com", "ramiltonsfinance.com"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.t1555.003

logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:

            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'

            - '\opera.exe'

falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

let BadHashes = dynamic(["44f4f7aca7f1d9bfdaf7b3736934cbe19f851a707662f8f0b0c49b383e054250", "332ba2f0297dfb1599adecc3e9067893e7cf243aa23aedce4906a4c480574c17", "0db36a04d304ad96f9e6f97b531934594cd95a5cea9ff2c9af249201089dc864", "38bd137c672bd58d08c4f0502f993a6561e2c3411773d1ae57ee0151a0a9d11d", "d4a7e9f107fe40c1a5d0139c6c6e25bf6bf57f61feff090bee28f476bb3cc3c2", "bc3b44154518c5794ce639108e7b9c5fecb0c189607a26de1aaed518d890c7ad", "74882085db2088356ed7f72f01e0404a0a98cda88ef56fb15ce74c1f36b26d27", "9cf029daca89523d917dafed0568d11d00e45ec96b5b90b4a1f7fd4018c7da84", "b19e06da580cf91691eda066ac9ee4b09c6e5dc26c367af12660fe1f9306eec4", "8808c794c24367438f183e4be941876f1d3ecd0c8d2eb43b10d2380841d2283b", "43dc62cef52ebdd69e79f10015b3e13890f26c058325c0ff139c70f8d8eadcfa", "9e4a658e6d831c9e9bdfe11884a75b7c64812ed0a80e8495ddf6b316505acac1"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
—
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] Vulnerable UniFi OS devices exposed to CVE-2026-34908/34909/34910/33000/34911
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] Vulnerable UniFi OS devices exposed to CVE-2026-34908/34909/34910/33000/34911 Weaponization High
Surfaces managed UniFi OS / UDM / UNVR / UNAS / UCG assets carrying any of the five May-2026 critical CVEs (three CVSS 10.0 plus the additional critical command-injection and information-disclosure flaws). Article-specific because all five CVE IDs are unique to this Ubiquiti advisory bundle; pivots straight from threat-intel to assets that still need patching. Rationale: All seven CVE IDs come directly from the Bleeping Computer article (CVE-2026-34908/34909/34910 plus CVE-2026-33000/34911 patched the same week, and CVE-2026-22557/22558 from the March bundle). Cross-checked against securityonline.info, stack.watch and TheHackerWire for affected SKUs (UDM/UDM-Pro/UDM-SE/UDM-Pro-Max < 5.1.12, UniFi OS Server < 5.0.8, UCG/UNVR/UNAS) which informed the SoftwareName allowlist. Censys reported ~100K internet-exposed UniFi endpoints, so IsInternetFacing is the priority pivot. Cross-checked against: • https://securityonline.info/ubiquiti-unifi-os-critical-vulnerabilities-cvss-10-firmware-update/ • https://stack.watch/vuln/CVE-2026-34909/ • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-34908 • https://www.scworld.com/brief/ubiquiti-patches-three-critical-vulnerabilities-in-unifi-os
ATT&CKT1190 T1133

   or (SoftwareVendor =~ "ubiquiti" and SoftwareName has_any ("unifi os","udm","unvr","unas","ucg","unifi network"))

| order by LastSeen desc

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-34908", "CVE-2026-34909", "CVE-2026-34910", "CVE-2026-33000", "CVE-2026-34911", "CVE-2026-22557", "CVE-2026-22558")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-34908", "CVE-2026-34909", "CVE-2026-34910", "CVE-2026-33000", "CVE-2026-34911", "CVE-2026-22557", "CVE-2026-22558")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
